title: Non-contrast MRI reliably captures perfusion abnormalities in status epilepticus.
abstract: Objective To determine whether non-contrast pseudo-continuous arterial spin labeling (pCASL) detects status epilepticus (SE)-related perfusion abnormalities and shows quantitative correspondence with dynamic susceptibility contrast (DSC) perfusion magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and to compare single-slice and volumetric approaches for asymmetry assessment. Methods Adult patients from a prospectively recruited single-center SE cohort were included in this retrospective analysis when MRI was performed within 48 h after clinical SE onset and both pCASL and DSC perfusion sequences were available. Visual assessment was pCASL-led, with corresponding DSC-derived cerebral blood flow (CBF) and cerebral blood volume (CBV) maps subsequently evaluated. Perfusion asymmetry was quantified using mirrored contralateral reference regions. Single-slice peak-abnormality and volumetric segmentation approaches were applied to pCASL, DSC-derived cerebral blood flow (CBF), and cerebral blood volume (CBV). Results Of 982 individuals with SE, 180 underwent MRI including pCASL and DSC within 48 h. pCASL-led assessment identified SE-related perfusion abnormalities in 75 of 180 (42%): hyperperfusion in 65, hypoperfusion in 6, and pCASL-DSC discordance in 4. Corresponding DSC abnormalities were present in 71 of 75 (95%). Thus, quantitative asymmetry analysis was performed in 71 unilateral evaluable cases. In the hyperperfusion subgroup, pCASL asymmetry correlated significantly with DSC-derived CBF using both volumetric and single-slice assessment (ρ = .558 and ρ = .571, respectively; both p < .001), and with DSC-derived CBV (ρ = .495 and ρ = .374, respectively; p < .001 and p = .003). Single-slice and volumetric pCASL asymmetry showed strong correspondence (ρ = .773, p < .001). No significant difference was observed between single-slice and volumetric pCASL asymmetry after correction for multiple comparisons. Significance Non-contrast pCASL detected SE-related peri-ictal perfusion abnormalities and showed significant quantitative correspondence with DSC-derived CBF and CBV in parenchymal hyperperfusion. Single-slice pCASL asymmetry showed strong agreement with volumetric assessment, supporting its use as a pragmatic approach for clinically oriented evaluation.

Methods

Adult patients from a prospectively recruited single-center SE cohort were included in this retrospective analysis when MRI was performed within 48 h after clinical SE onset and both pCASL and DSC perfusion sequences were available. Visual assessment was pCASL-led, with corresponding DSC-derived cerebral blood flow (CBF) and cerebral blood volume (CBV) maps subsequently evaluated. Perfusion asymmetry was quantified using mirrored contralateral reference regions. Single-slice peak-abnormality and volumetric segmentation approaches were applied to pCASL, DSC-derived cerebral blood flow (CBF), and cerebral blood volume (CBV).

Results

Of 982 individuals with SE, 180 underwent MRI including pCASL and DSC within 48 h. pCASL-led assessment identified SE-related perfusion abnormalities in 75 of 180 (42%): hyperperfusion in 65, hypoperfusion in 6, and pCASL-DSC discordance in 4. Corresponding DSC abnormalities were present in 71 of 75 (95%). Thus, quantitative asymmetry analysis was performed in 71 unilateral evaluable cases. In the hyperperfusion subgroup, pCASL asymmetry correlated significantly with DSC-derived CBF using both volumetric and single-slice assessment (ρ = .558 and ρ = .571, respectively; both p < .001), and with DSC-derived CBV (ρ = .495 and ρ = .374, respectively; p < .001 and p = .003). Single-slice and volumetric pCASL asymmetry showed strong correspondence (ρ = .773, p < .001). No significant difference was observed between single-slice and volumetric pCASL asymmetry after correction for multiple comparisons.

Significance

Non-contrast pCASL detected SE-related peri-ictal perfusion abnormalities and showed significant quantitative correspondence with DSC-derived CBF and CBV in parenchymal hyperperfusion. Single-slice pCASL asymmetry showed strong agreement with volumetric assessment, supporting its use as a pragmatic approach for clinically oriented evaluation.

title: Stereoelectroencephalography-guided radiofrequency thermocoagulation in drug-resistant focal epilepsy: Results from more than 20 years of experience.
abstract: Objective This study was undertaken to present more than 2 decades of experience with stereoelectroencephalography (SEEG)-guided radiofrequency thermocoagulation (RF-TC) in focal drug-resistant epilepsy and to identify clinical, electrophysiological, and procedural predictors of treatment response. Methods We retrospectively studied 244 consecutive patients treated with SEEG-guided RF-TC at our center between 2001 and 2024. All had at least 2 months of follow-up, and 240 (98.4%) completed 1 year. Outcomes were assessed at 2, 6, and 12 months. The primary endpoint was seizure freedom at 2 months and 1 year without additional surgery, and the secondary endpoint was ≥50% seizure reduction. title: Deep whole genome sequencing of epileptogenic brain lesions.
abstract: Objective Malformations of cortical development and low-grade epilepsy-associated tumors often cause drug-resistant lesional focal epilepsy (LFE) amenable to surgical treatment. Genetic testing of resected brain tissue can provide diagnostic and mechanistic information and may eventually support personalized treatment approaches. However, systematic >300× whole genome sequencing (GS) of bulk epileptogenic lesions, particularly after nondiagnostic deep exome sequencing and array-based genotyping, has not been evaluated. Methods Here, we performed deep GS (>300× coverage) on 33 epileptogenic brain lesions from individuals with LFE, selected for lesions with a high prior probability of a genetic finding, all of whom had negative results for candidate germline or somatic variants in previous deep exome sequencing (ES; >350× coverage) and array-based genotyping. Results We identified candidate somatic variants in known LFE-associated genes in seven of 33 participants (21%). Two participants had two candidate variants each. In total, three of 33 participants (9%) had variants that could only be detected by GS: two deletions in TSC2, two deletions in NPRL3, and an exonic inversion in FGFR1. Three individuals had germline polymorphisms that may represent modulators or risk factors. Exploratory mutational signature analysis revealed clocklike signatures and a correlation between mutational signatures, age at seizure onset, and histopathology, indicating an age-related mechanism of mutation. Significance Deep GS establishes the feasibility of genome-wide profiling at a depth relevant to low-variant allelic frequency mosaicism and reveals candidate variants missed by ES, particularly complex structural variants. As sequencing costs decrease, GS may complement other technologies in somatic variant detection, enabling more widespread clinical implementation of tissue sequencing in epilepsy surgery. Further studies are needed to address the remaining conceptual and technological challenges in somatic variant detection.

title: Multimodal modeling of the ictal onset zone in refractory insular epilepsy and seizure outcome of magnetic resonance-guided laser interstitial therapy: A pediatric single-center retrospective study.
abstract: Objective This study was undertaken to evaluate seizure outcomes after magnetic resonance-guided laser interstitial thermal therapy (MRgLITT) in children with insular epilepsy and to assess how the extent of ablation overlaps with multimodal definitions of the ictal onset zone (IOZ). Methods We conducted a retrospective, single-center study including consecutive pediatric patients treated with MRgLITT for insular epilepsy. All patients underwent presurgical evaluation including electroencephalography (EEG) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI); fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography (FDG-PET) and stereo-EEG (SEEG) were performed in negative-MRI cases. Epileptic zone was identified by visual analysis of SEEG recording. Postablation contrast-enhancing volumes were manually segmented and coregistered with IOZ estimates derived from Multi-centre Epilepsy Lesion Detection (MELD) MRI analysis, FDG-PET voxel-based analysis, and the Epileptogenicity Index, when available. Spatial concordance between modalities was assessed using Dice similarity coefficients, and the proportion of each IOZ modality encompassed within the ablation volume was correlated with postoperative seizure outcomes (International League Against Epilepsy classification). Results Eight children (median age = 10.4 years, range = 2.3-17) were included, with a median postoperative follow-up of 38 months. Two patients had insular tumors, and both achieved seizure freedom after complete ablation. Among the six MRI-negative patients, FDG-PET revealed insular hypometabolism in four, MELD detected a median of one insular cluster (range 1-3), and SEEG identified focal insular ictal activity in three cases. Overall, four negative-MRI patients achieved seizure freedom: three after MRgLITT alone and one after MRgLITT combined with frontal opercular resection. One transient postoperative aphasia was observed. Intermodality spatial concordance was low across all comparisons. A greater proportion of FDG-PET hypometabolism included in the ablation volume was associated with better seizure outcomes (p = .012). Significance MRgLITT is an effective and safe treatment option for focal insular epilepsy in children, either as standalone therapy or in a combined approach. Optimal outcome depends on accurate preoperative delineation of the IOZ and its complete ablation.

title: Brain volumetric signatures of neighborhood disadvantage in focal epilepsy.
abstract: Objective Social disadvantage is an important determinant of health in focal epilepsy, but its neurobiological basis remains unclear. We examined whether brain morphometric alterations represent a structural signature of deprivation. Methods We performed a retrospective cohort study of 340 adults with pharmacoresistant focal epilepsy evaluated at the Cleveland Clinic (2010-2022). Age- and sex-adjusted volumetric percentiles were derived from 3-T brain magnetic resonance imaging. To account for hemispheric network differences, analyses were stratified by epilepsy laterality (right vs. left), adjusting for seizure localization, seizure burden, and lesional status. Neighborhood disadvantage was quantified using the Area Deprivation Index (ADI) and categorized into low, moderate, and high deprivation using the R sociome package. To identify coordinated structural patterns, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression with 10-fold cross-validation was applied to high-dimensional volumetric data, followed by latent Dirichlet allocation (LDA) to derive latent volumetric networks. Associations between network expression and ADI were assessed using Spearman correlation and Kruskal-Wallis with false discovery rate (FDR) correction. Regional patterns were visualized using ggseg. Results In right-sided epilepsy, LDA-derived networks were significantly associated with ADI (FDR p = .01). title: Neurometabolite abnormalities and associations with epilepsy duration and cognition in patients with idiopathic generalized epilepsies.
abstract: Objective This study investigated whether idiopathic generalized epilepsies (IGEs) are associated with neuroinflammation by measuring neurometabolite levels and brain temperature using whole-brain magnetic resonance spectroscopy imaging (MRSI). We compared patients with IGEs to healthy controls (HCs), and in IGEs examined relationships with seizure control, MRSI markers, epilepsy duration, and cognitive performance. Methods Seventeen patients with IGEs and 15 HCs underwent 3T-MRI scans. IGEs were also administered the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) and Flanker test. Whole-brain 1 H-MRSI provided metabolite and water maps. Levels for myo-inositol (MI; glial marker), glutamate-glutamine complex (Glx), and N-acetylaspartate (NAA) were normalized to creatine (Cr) levels. Brain temperature was obtained by frequency difference between water and Cr. IGEs were stratified into seizure-free (IGE-) and treatment-resistant (IGE+) groups. Group analyses were performed using permutation-based threshold-free cluster enhancement (TFCE) within bilateral regions of interest: anterior cingulate cortex (ACC), posterior cingulate cortex (PCC), hippocampus, parietal cortex, and thalami. Results Compared with HCs, IGEs showed higher MI/Cr in the parietal cortex, PCC, and thalamus; higher hippocampus Glx/Cr; and lower parietal cortex NAA/Cr. Brain temperature did not differ between groups. IGE- exhibited higher hippocampal NAA/Cr and better MoCA scores than IGE+. Longer epilepsy duration was associated with lower NAA/Cr in the ACC and PCC, and parietal cortex, as well as lower Glx/Cr in the ACC, PCC, parietal cortex, and hippocampus. Lower NAA/Cr in the ACC, PCC, hippocampus, and thalamus, together with higher thalamus MI/Cr, was associated with lower MoCA scores in IGEs. Lower NAA/Cr in the ACC, thalamus, and hippocampus was associated with poorer Flanker performance in IGEs. Significance We provide novel evidence of neurometabolic abnormalities in IGEs. The associations between metabolite levels and clinical and cognitive variables suggest potential biomarkers for disease progression and treatment response. Furthermore, these results highlight the roles of abnormal glial activation, neuronal loss, and hyperexcitability in IGE pathophysiology. We found group differences in brain N-acetylaspartate (NAA; neuronal marker), myo-inositol (MI; glial cell marker), and glutamate/glutamine (Glx; excitatory neurotransmission) levels, but not in brain temperature. Longer epilepsy duration was associated with brain chemistry levels. In IGEs, lower NAA levels and higher MI levels were associated with worse cognitive performance. This study highlights the roles of abnormal glial activation, neuronal loss, and hyperexcitability in epilepsy duration and cognition in IGEs.

title: Reversal of refractory epilepsy in an adult with GAMT deficiency: A case report and comparative literature review.
abstract: Objective Guanidinoacetate methyltransferase (GAMT) deficiency is a rare autosomal recessive creatine biosynthesis disorder. Reports specifically focusing on adult patients remain scarce. Methods We report a 52-year-old female (the oldest documented case of GAMT deficiency to date) presenting with severe intellectual disability, refractory epilepsy, and adult-onset disease progression. Whole-exome sequencing identified novel compound heterozygous GAMT variants (c.265_267del and c.253G>T), and magnetic resonance spectroscopy confirmed cerebral creatine depletion. Remarkably, initiating oral creatine supplementation at age 52 achieved complete seizure freedom, normalization of the electroencephalogram (EEG), and significant motor function recovery. Results A comprehensive review revealed that untreated adult patients face a high risk of progressive neurological deterioration. Compared to the pediatric cohort, adults exhibited a significantly higher prevalence of movement disorders (69.2% vs. 33.1%, p < 0.001) and a trend toward a higher prevalence of epilepsy (92.3% vs. 74.2%). Especially, atonic seizures (drop attacks) are particularly characteristic of adult GAMT deficiency, with EEGs frequently demonstrating background slowing, multifocal epileptiform discharges, and electrodecremental patterns. Significance This study underscores that continuous disease progression and prolonged neurotoxicity still could compromise the well-being of adult GAMT deficiency patients. Accurate diagnosis is essential for adults presenting with developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (DEE) phenotype, as even late treatment for GAMT deficiency can still dramatically alleviate the epileptic burden and reverse motor decline. Plain language summary We report the oldest known adult diagnosed with GAMT deficiency. Our case demonstrates that starting creatine treatment even at age 52 can dramatically reduce seizures and restore motor function. Literature shows that untreated adults suffer from more severe epilepsy and movement disorders than children, with symptoms worsening over time. These findings highlight the critical need for genetic testing in adults with unexplained severe epilepsy; timely creatine supplementation can halt cognitive decline and significantly restore quality of life.

title: Progressive Hippocampal Volume Reduction Beyond Normal Aging in Temporal Lobe Epilepsy: A Longitudinal MRI Study.
abstract: Recent neuroimaging studies have suggested that epilepsy may show progressive brain structural changes over time. However, longitudinal hippocampal volume changes in temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE) have not been adequately compared with those observed in normal aging. In this study, we enrolled 46 patients with unilateral TLE and 25 healthy controls with longitudinal structural MRI scans using the same scanner. Hippocampal volumes were quantified using the Hipposeg software, and the annual percentage volume reduction relative to baseline (%Reduction/year) was calculated for each hippocampus. Compared to healthy hippocampi (median -0.37% per year, IQR = 3.97), both ipsilateral (median -1.04% per year, IQR = 3.65) and contralateral (median -1.08% per year, IQR = 3.17) hippocampi in TLE showed significantly greater volume reduction over time (both p < 0.05). Furthermore, annual ipsilateral hippocampal volume reduction was significantly correlated with disease duration (Spearman's rs = 0.366, FDR-corrected p = 0.036), suggesting that hippocampal atrophy progresses more rapidly during the early stage after epilepsy onset. These findings indicate that hippocampal volume loss in TLE exceeds that expected from normal aging and provide further evidence supporting progressive structural alterations during the course of the disease. PLAIN LANGUAGE SUMMARY: Temporal lobe epilepsy may cause progressive changes in the brain beyond those expected from normal aging. Using repeated MRI scans, we found that the hippocampus showed greater volume loss over time in people with temporal lobe epilepsy than in healthy individuals. This volume loss occurred bilaterally and appeared to be greater during the earlier stages of the disease. These results provide further evidence supporting progressive structural brain changes in TLE and contribute to a better understanding of disease progression and abnormal brain aging in epilepsy.

title: Charting the Normal Development of Structural Brain Connectivity in Utero Using Diffusion MRI.
abstract: Understanding the structural connectivity of the human brain during fetal life is critical for uncovering the early foundations of neural function and vulnerability to developmental disorders. Diffusion-weighted MRI (dMRI) enables non-invasive mapping of white matter pathways and construction of the brain's structural connectome, but its application to the fetal brain has been limited by data scarcity and technical difficulties in analyzing fetal dMRI data. Here, we present the largest study to date of in utero brain connectivity, analyzing high-quality dMRI data from 198 fetuses between 22 and 37 gestational weeks from the Developing Human Connectome Project. We employed advanced fetal-specific tools for brain segmentation and parcellation, and used ensemble tractography to encourage more complete reconstruction of various white matter tracts. For connection weighting, we relied on the notion of fiber bundle capacity. We reconstructed individual structural connectomes and characterized the developmental trajectories. Graph-theoretical analysis revealed consistent increases in integration and segregation metrics over gestation, while bootstrapping confirmed the robustness of nodal and edge-wise developmental patterns. Furthermore, we proposed a novel method for constructing age-specific connectome templates based on aggregation of individual subject connectomes. The new method follows an optimization-based approach to ensure that the connectome templates closely represent individual subject connectomes, are temporally consistent, and proportionally preserve short and long connections. Our analysis shows that this approach is superior to spatial alignment and averaging of the data in image space, with the resulting connectome templates supporting accurate prediction of the gestational age of individual fetuses (mean error = 0.90±0.81 weeks). In summary, this study provides robust normative benchmarks for fetal brain structural connectivity and demonstrates that connectome-based measures capture meaningful developmental signatures, offering a framework for future studies of early brain development.

title: DTI-ALPS as a Biomarker of Small Vessel Disease Progression and Amyloid-β in Normal Aging: A 3-Year Longitudinal Study.
abstract: Cerebral small vessel disease (SVD) is a leading cause of stroke, vascular cognitive impairment, and functional decline in older adults. Emerging experimental and translational data implicate glymphatic dysfunction in SVD pathogenesis and in vascular amyloid accumulation. The analysis along the perivascular space (ALPS) index, derived from diffusion tensor imaging (DTI), noninvasively estimates water diffusivity along perivascular pathways and has been proposed as an indirect imaging marker related to glymphatic function. In this study, we aim to determine whether the baseline DTI-ALPS index is associated with baseline SVD burden and subsequent longitudinal changes in SVD markers and amyloid-β deposition in cognitively normal aging. We analyzed 204 cognitively normal participants from the Harvard Aging Brain Study with baseline and follow-up visits separated by 3 years. Primary MRI SVD outcomes were intracranial-volume-normalized white matter hyperintensities (WMH/ICV), and visual SVD ratings (Fazekas, ARWMC, perivascular space, and BOMBS [microbleed scale]). Secondary outcomes included cortical amyloid PET burden (PIB_FS_DVR_FLR). We tested the effects of time, baseline ALPS (z-scored), and the time-ALPS interaction using Bayesian mixed-effects models with subject-specific random intercepts adjusted for baseline age, sex, and education; amyloid models were additionally adjusted for APOE4 status. Continuous outcomes were modeled with Gaussian mixed-effects models, binary outcomes with Bernoulli mixed-effects models, and ordinal outcomes with Bayesian cumulative mixed-effects models. In a sensitivity analysis, ALPS was recalculated after excluding voxels with λ 2 /λ 3 > 1.8, and the models were repeated using the crossing-fiber-adjusted index. Posterior means and 95% HDIs were the primary summaries. Multiplicity was controlled using the Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate procedure, and the resulting FDR-adjusted two-sided posterior tail-area p-analogues are reported as p corrected . Over the 3-year follow-up, SVD and amyloid-β burden increased: WMH/ICV (β = 0.096, 95% HDI [0.069, 0.121], p corrected < 0.001), cortical amyloid-β (β = 0.130, 95% HDI [0.106, 0.152], p corrected < 0.001), Fazekas (β = 0.320, 95% HDI [0.088, 0.541], p corrected = 0.010), ARWMC (β = 0.404, 95% HDI [0.165, 0.649], p corrected = 0.004), basal ganglia (β = 0.318, 95% HDI [0.079, 0.546], p corrected = 0.010), and centrum semiovale (β = 0.244, 95% HDI [0.026, 0.450], p corrected = 0.025). PVS scores also increased over time. Higher baseline ALPS was associated with lower Fazekas severity (β = -0.742, 95% HDI [-1.281, -0.201], p corrected = 0.026) and with attenuated amyloid accumulation over time (β = -0.025, 95% HDI [-0.049, -0.001], p corrected = 0.039). title: Charting Cervical Spinal Cord Morphometry Across the Lifespan.
abstract: Spinal cord morphometry provides essential biomarkers of neurological health, but clinical interpretations are confounded by inter-subject variability and a lack of normative references across the full human lifespan. We address this gap by generating the first comprehensive lifespan charts for cervical spinal cord morphometry. From 78,269 T1-weighted brain MRI sessions, we identified a final cross-sectional cohort of 24,251 healthy or cognitively normal controls from 33 datasets (ages 0-100 years) with cervical cord coverage. To overcome contrast variability, we employed a state-of-the-art contrast-agnostic deep learning segmentation method, extracting cross-sectional area (CSA), anteroposterior (AP) and right-left (RL/transverse), and shape indices (AP/RL ratio, eccentricity, and solidity) from C1 to C7. Normative trajectories were modeled using Generalized Additive Models for Location, Scale, and Shape (GAMLSS). The resulting charts reveal distinct non-linear lifespan changes: rapid growth through childhood and adolescence, peak maturation occurring in early-to-mid adulthood (e.g., mid-30s for CSA), followed by gradual decreases. Significant regional variations along the cervical cord and consistent sex differences (males > females for size metrics) were quantified. Spinal cord trajectories showed strong temporal coupling with brain white matter and brainstem volumes, suggesting integrated CNS development and aging. These lifespan charts provide a robust normative framework, enabling age- and sex-specific centile scoring of individual spinal cord morphometry. This resource offers a critical tool for differentiating typical variation from pathological changes, enhancing the clinical utility of spinal cord MRI in studies of development and neurodegeneration.

title: A Computed Tomography Radiomics Approach for Assessing the T Cell-Inflamed Gene Expression Profile in Hepatocellular Carcinoma and Its Association With Immunotherapy Response.
abstract: Background The T cell-inflamed gene expression profile (GEP) provides a biomarker for immunotherapy response across various cancers. However, specific biomarkers for immunotherapy response in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) are lacking. In this study, we established a computed tomography (CT)-based radiomics model to predict the T cell-inflamed GEP and immunotherapy response in HCC. Methods This retrospective, multicenter study included 270 patients with HCC, who were divided into training ( n = 227) and test sets ( n = 43). All included patients had available contrast-enhanced CT and RNA sequencing data. The T cell-inflamed GEP consisted of 18 genes derived from RNA sequencing data, and patients were classified into GEP-high and GEP-low groups. A support vector machine was used to establish the radiomics model. The immunotherapy dataset comprised patients who underwent contrast-enhanced CT and received anti-programmed cell death protein 1/programmed cell death ligand 1 immunotherapy at three hospitals (209 lesions). This immunotherapy dataset was used to evaluate the association between the predicted GEP status and immunotherapy response. Additionally, overall survival was compared between patients with and without predicted GEP-high lesions in the immunotherapy dataset. Results The areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve of the radiomics model for predicting GEP in the training and test sets were 0.824 (95% confidence interval [CI] = 0.757-0.892) and 0.827 (95% CI: 0.674-0.980), respectively. In the immunotherapy dataset, the response rate of liver lesions at 6 months was significantly higher in the GEP-high group than in the GEP-low group (48.1% vs . 9.3%, p < 0.001). The areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve of the radiomics model for predicting immunotherapy response at 6 months was 0.750 (95% CI: 0.614-0.886). Median overall survival among patients with GEP-high lesions was 17.5 months, which notably exceeded the value of 8.3 months for patients without GEP-high lesions. Conclusions This study provides the first CT-based radiomics model for predicting the T cell-inflamed GEP in HCC. This model highlights the potential of the T cell-inflamed GEP as a noninvasive biomarker to help guide immunotherapy selection.

title: Prognostic Outcomes Following Endovascular Management for Carotid Blowout Syndrome: A Multi-Institutional Observational Cohort Study.
abstract: Background Carotid blowout syndrome (CBS) is a life-threatening complication of head and neck cancer (HNC). This study evaluated clinical outcomes and prognostic factors in patients with HNC who presented to the emergency department (ED) with CBS and underwent endovascular management. Methods We conducted a retrospective, multi-institutional observational study across four hospitals in Taiwan from January 1, 2011, to December 31, 2023. Adult patients with HNC who presented to the ED with bleeding suggestive of CBS on computed tomography angiography underwent endovascular therapy and had the diagnosis confirmed by digital subtraction angiography were included. The primary endpoint was in-hospital mortality. Independent prognostic factors were identified using multivariable logistic regression, and a predictive nomogram was constructed and internally validated by bootstrap resampling. Results A total of 348 patients were included. Most were male (93.7%), had Stage IV disease (74.7%), and were treated with arterial embolization (93.4%). title: Long-Term Outcomes of IDH2-Mutant Sinonasal Carcinomas Compared With IDH2-Wild Type Sinonasal Undifferentiated Carcinoma.
abstract: Background Sinonasal carcinomas are aggressive and often locally invasive at presentation, with no universally accepted treatment approach. Histopathologic IDH2-mutant status appears to be associated with improved treatment response and survival. However, the clinical significance of histopathologic classification among IDH2-mutant sinonasal carcinomas, as well as that of IDH2 mutation status within SNUC, remains unclear and long-term clinical outcome data are limited. Methods Records from a prospectively maintained skull-base database at a large, tertiary care hospital system from 1986 to 2024 were reviewed. Patients with a diagnosis of SNUC or sinonasal tumor of any histopathology positive for IDH2 R172 mutation were identified. SMARCB1-deficient, SMARCA4-deficient, NUT sinonasal carcinomas, and other small round cell mimickers were excluded. After histopathologic confirmation, 22 IDH2-mutant SNUC, 14 IDH2-mutant non-SNUC, and 8 IDH2-wildtype SNUC cases were amenable to comprehensive clinicopathologic data review. A presence of IDH2 R172 and pathogenic TP53 mutations was determined by molecular testing and/or by immunohistochemistry. Results The median age at diagnosis was 58 years and 61% of patients were male. The majority of patients presented with T4b disease (41% of IDH2-mutant SNUC; 57% of IDH2-mutant non-SNUC; 75% of IDH2-wildtype SNUC; p = 0.3). There was no significant difference in the proportion of patients presenting with orbital invasion (55% IDH2-mutant SNUC; 64% IDH2-mutant non-SNUC; 75% of IDH2-wildtype SNUC; p = 0.7) or intracranial invasion (82% IDH2-mutant SNUC; 79% IDH2-mutant non-SNUC; 75% of IDH2-wildtype SNUC; p = 0.7). On histopathology, there was no significant difference in perineural invasion and margin status between the three subgroups (p > 0.6). A greater proportion of IDH2-mutant non-SNUCs had TP53 mutations (67%) than IDH2-mutant SNUC (31%) and IDH2-wildtype SNUC (29%) (p = 0.13). Across the cohort, 41% of patients received neoadjuvant chemotherapy, with a partial response by RECIST criteria in 94% of patients across the subgroups. Median follow-up was 28 months (IQR 11-64 months). 5-year DSS of 73% in IDH2-mutant SNUC, 75% in IDH2-mutant non-SNUC and 80% in IDH2-wildtype SNUC (p = 0.78). 5-year RFS was 53% in IDH2-mutant SNUC, 48% in IDH2-mutant non-SNUC and 43% in IDH2-wildtype SNUC (p = 0.78). Conclusion Upfront assessment of IDH2 mutation status in sinonasal carcinoma patients may be warranted to select patients for clinical trials with IDH-inhibitors. However, no significant differences in the extent of disease at presentation or response to induction chemotherapy were observed according to histopathologic classification among IDH2-mutant sinonasal carcinomas or IDH2 mutation status within SNUC. Larger series are required to determine the prognostic significance of IDH2 mutation status in sinonasal carcinoma patients.

title: Newly diagnosed and relapsed follicular lymphoma: EHA Clinical Practice Guidelines for diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up.
abstract: Follicular lymphoma (FL) is the second most common lymphoma subtype in Europe, with a median age at diagnosis of 60-65 years. It is generally considered an indolent disease, and the median overall survival at diagnosis now likely exceeds 20 years. However, considerable heterogeneity exists. Diagnosis requires adequate biopsy material and a specialized hematopathologist. Staging and prognosis rely on positron emission tomography (PET)-computed tomography (CT). Prognostication at diagnosis is based on several validated clinical prognostic scores. Localized disease is usually treated with radiotherapy ± Rituximab. The treatment of disseminated disease includes active surveillance (or in selected cases Rituximab monotherapy) for low-tumor burden patients, and most often immunochemotherapy (or in selected cases chemo-free therapeutic options), ±antibody maintenance in high-tumor burden patients. For relapsed or refractory disease, treatment with Rituximab-Lenalidomide combination ± Tafasitamab or Epcoritamab from the first relapse and single-agent bispecific antibodies, chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapy (CAR-T) cells, and Zanubrutinib-Obinutuzumab after second relapse should be prioritized over immunochemotherapy. Given the long natural history and risk of relapse, careful follow-up is an important part of patient management. Patients should be actively involved in decision-making. In this guideline, we present current evidence-based recommendations for diagnosis, staging, treatment, and follow-up.

title: Harmonized Protocol for Segmentation of the Hippocampal Tail on High-Resolution In Vivo MRI From the Hippocampal Subfields Group (HSG).
abstract: The hippocampus is a heterogeneous structure with cytoarchitectonically distinct subfields that exhibit heterogeneous lifespan trajectories and are differentially susceptible to diseases. Advances in high-resolution imaging have accelerated research on these structures, yet variability in segmentation protocols limits cross-study comparability. The Hippocampal Subfields Group (HSG) is an international consortium addressing this challenge by developing a reliable, accessible, and freely available segmentation protocol for high-resolution T2-weighted 3T MRI scans (http://www.hippocampalsubfields.com). Here, we present the harmonized protocol for the posterior portion of the hippocampus (the "tail"), complementing the previously established "body" protocol, and with an anterior "head" protocol under development. The tail protocol provides standardized definitions of the external boundaries for the posterior-most extent of the hippocampus, facilitating consistent segmentation from surrounding tissues. The research community was extensively involved through an online survey that incorporated comprehensive protocol details, feasibility assessments, tutorial videos, and illustrative segmentations. Through this collaborative process, consensus emerged to exclude subfield labeling in the hippocampal tail due to limited visibility of internal landmarks and substantial anatomical variability in this region. All proposed boundary guidelines were deemed clear and agreed upon via a Delphi procedure. The harmonized tail protocol has high intra- (Averaged ICC(2, 1) > 0.98; Averaged Dice Similarity Coefficient = 0.92) and inter-rater reliability (Averaged ICC(2, k) > 0.98; Averaged Dice Similarity Coefficient = 0.86) and offers a practical framework for replicable segmentation. By establishing standardized guidelines, this protocol enhances comparability of findings across developmental, aging, and clinical research and is compatible with ongoing technological advances.

title: Diagnostic Performance of Color Doppler Ultrasound for Detecting Nuchal Cord and Associated Immediate Neonatal Outcomes at Term in Uganda: A Prospective Diagnostic-Accuracy Cohort Study.
abstract: Background and aims Evidence on the diagnostic performance of color Doppler ultrasound for detecting nuchal cord and its association with immediate neonatal outcomes remains limited in sub-Saharan Africa. We evaluated ultrasound detection of nuchal cord and compared immediate neonatal outcomes according to nuchal-cord status. Methods This prospective study included 246 women with singleton pregnancies at ≥ 37 weeks who were enrolled in early labor at Mbarara Regional Referral Hospital, Uganda, from February to July 2021. Two-dimensional and color Doppler ultrasound was performed at enrollment, and direct examination of the umbilical cord at delivery was the reference standard. Diagnostic-performance measures and unadjusted risk ratios (RRs) were reported with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Results Nuchal cord was confirmed at delivery in 88/246 participants in the sampled cohort. Ultrasound identified 76/88 participants with and 152/158 without a nuchal cord. Sensitivity was 86.4% (95% CI: 77.4-92.8), specificity 96.2% (95% CI: 91.9-98.6), positive predictive value 92.7% (95% CI: 84.8-97.3) and negative predictive value 92.7% (95% CI: 87.6-96.2). title: Advancing Early Breast Cancer Diagnosis and Ki-67 Expression Prediction With Ultrasound Viscoelastography: Based on Peritumoral Assessment.
abstract: Background Breast cancer is the most common invasive malignancy in women. Ultrasound viscoelastography may improve non-invasive diagnosis, but the clinical relevance of peritumoral viscoelastic parameters (VPs) and their correlation with Ki-67 remain unclear. This study explores these associations. Methods A prospective study enrolled 256 breast masses (156 malignant, 100 benign). Patients underwent conventional ultrasound and viscoelastography. VPs were acquired within masses (A), peritumoral shells (Shell1: 1 mm, Shell2: 2 mm, Shell3: 3 mm), and combined regions (A' = A + Shell). Quantitative metrics included elasticity (V/1 E, V/0 E), dispersion coefficient (V/1 D), viscosity coefficient (V/0 V), and their maximum (Max), minimum (Min), mean(Mean), and standard deviation (SD) values. Diagnostic performance was evaluated by analyzing the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve and calculating the area under the curve (AUC), followed by logistic regression. VPs were compared between high/low Ki-67 groups. Results The AUCs of peritumoral VPs exceeded those from masses. V/1 D showed higher AUC than V/0 V and elasticity values, with Shell3 V/1 D SD having the highest AUC (0.840). The diagnostic efficacy of the peritumoral viscoelastic model surpassed that of the single elasticity parameter model, with 89.1% sensitivity, 73% specificity, 82.8% accuracy. Key variables included Shell3 V/1 D and Shell3 V/0 E. Shell1 V/0 V Max was significantly higher in high versus low Ki-67 expression groups ( p < 0.05). Conclusion The viscoelastic model improves diagnostic accuracy by quantifying peritumoral biomechanics, and certain VPs may predict Ki-67 expression. Peritumoral VPs show potential as novel non-invasive imaging biomarkers for early breast cancer evaluation.

title: Histopathological Spectrum in FIT-Positive Patients With Abnormal Colonoscopy Findings at a Tertiary Medical Center in Lebanon: A Retrospective Observational Study.
abstract: Background and aims Colorectal cancer is a leading cause of cancer-related morbidity and mortality, and the prognosis significantly depends on the diagnostic stage. Various screening initiatives have been established, among which the fecal immunochemical test (FIT) (FITFIT) which is prominent for its affordability, non-invasive approach, and wide acceptance. This study aimed to describe the spectrum of histopathological findings among patients with positive fecal occult blood test and abnormal colonoscopy findings, and to identify associated risk factors. Methods This retrospective observational study included 172 adults with documented positive FIT and abnormal colonoscopy findings at Makassed General Hospital from January 2024 to December 2025. Statistical analysis was conducted using SPSS version 25, and associations were assessed using chi-square or Fisher's exact tests, with significance defined as p < 0.05. Results A total of 172 patients were included, with a mean age of 63.88 ± 11.79 years, and 55.2% were female. The most frequently recorded indications for colonoscopy were anemia (39%) and screening (37.2%). Polyps were the most common colonoscopy finding. Histopathological examination demonstrated that neoplastic polyps represented the predominant diagnosis (65.1%), followed by non-neoplastic lesions (24.4%) and malignancy (10.5%). Patients aged 45 years and older demonstrated a higher prevalence of polyps on colonoscopy; however, the difference did not reach statistical significance. No significant association was observed between gender and colonoscopy or histopathological findings. Abdominal pain and diarrhea were both significantly associated with non-neoplastic histopathological lesions. Conclusion Among patients with positive FIT and abnormal colonoscopy findings, neoplastic polyps rather than malignancy represented the predominant histopathological findings, supporting the clinical utility of FIT in detecting clinically important colorectal lesions at earlier stages. In addition, variability in the histopathology depending on the clinical presentation may contribute to clinical assessment and risk stratification. Larger prospective studies are needed to determine predictors of advanced colorectal histopathology.

title: Tumour Antigen-Specific Antibody Signatures as Diagnostic Biomarkers for Melanoma.
abstract: Early detection of melanoma remains challenging, and minimally invasive diagnostic tools are needed to complement imaging and histopathology. Circulating tumour antigen-specific antibodies (Abs) are promising biomarkers, but their diagnostic value across melanoma stages is not fully established. Circulating IgG and IgM Abs were profiled in plasma from two independent melanoma cohorts, early-stage (n = 65) and advanced-stage (n = 77), alongside healthy controls (n = 86) and individuals with prior cancer in remission (n = 37). A protein microarray containing 263 tumour antigens, predominantly cancer-testis (CT) antigens, was used to measure plasma antibody (Ab) reactivity. Univariate and multivariate ROC analyses identified candidate diagnostic biomarker signatures. Early-stage melanoma was best distinguished by an IgM signature comprising AURKA, BAGE3, BAGE4, CDK7, CEP290, MYBL2, PIAS2, RAD51 and SPANXB1 (AUC = 0.939). An IgG signature including ANKRD45, BCL2L14, CDK2, MAGEA4v3, MAPK3 and RBM46 achieved AUC = 0.827. Advanced-stage melanoma exhibited broader Ab repertoires, including an IgG signature (CTAG1A, DKKL1, PIWIL2, SPANXN1, TSGA10, TSPY1; AUC = 0.865) and an IgM signature (CPXCR1, CSAG2, FMR1NB, FOXR2, LIPI, MAGEA5, TSGA10; AUC = 0.889). Individuals in cancer remission displayed persistent Ab signatures distinct from early melanoma and healthy controls. Overlap between IgG and IgM repertoires was minimal, highlighting complementary discriminatory value. Circulating IgG and IgM Abs against tumour antigens reveal stage-specific signatures that distinguish melanoma from healthy individuals and those in cancer remission, identifying candidate discovery-stage diagnostic biomarker signatures warranting independent validation in larger prospective cohorts to determine clinical utility.

title: Reinterpreting cervical cerclage classification: Diagnostic detection and operative context.
abstract: Cervical cerclage is conventionally classified as history-indicated, ultrasound-indicated, or examination-indicated cerclage, the latter often performed as emergency cervical cerclage. These categories remain clinically useful because they describe common pathways of risk recognition, surveillance, intervention, and rescue. However, they are sometimes interpreted as biologically uniform or sequential stages of cervical insufficiency. This narrative review examines the historical and diagnostic basis of the conventional classification and focuses on its limitations for describing emergency cerclage. The three categories can also be understood as reflecting how and when cervical vulnerability becomes detectable: through antecedent obstetric history, sonographic cervical change, or physical examination findings. This interpretation does not diminish the importance of obstetric history or imply that ultrasound surveillance should delay preventive intervention. Rather, history and surveillance are complementary routes to timely recognition. In emergency cerclage, indication labels alone do not describe membrane exposure or prolapse, membrane reducibility, residual cervical tissue, procedural feasibility, or operative configuration. Therefore, we propose retaining the established indication-based classification while supplementing it with structured reporting of detection timing and operative context. This reporting approach might improve interpretation and comparability of emergency cerclage studies without replacing established clinical terminology.

title: Non-invasive diagnosis of endometriosis: From expert imaging to molecular and artificial intelligence-enabled pathways.
abstract: Endometriosis affects approximately one in 10 women and people assigned female at birth of reproductive age, yet diagnosis is still delayed by years, historically because confirmation required laparoscopy. This review synthesizes which non-invasive tools-expert ultrasound and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), molecular and microRNA (miRNA) biomarkers, and artificial intelligence (AI)-are ready for clinical use and which have so far been evaluated only in research settings and proposes a pragmatic clinical pathway. This is a narrative review and not a systematic review. Major guidelines now endorse a clinical and imaging-based diagnosis without mandatory laparoscopy. Expert transvaginal ultrasound and MRI identify ovarian endometrioma and deep endometriosis with high specificity and map disease for surgery, but a normal scan does not exclude endometriosis because superficial peritoneal endometriosis remains largely invisible. No blood, urinary, or endometrial biomarker meets criteria for clinical use; circulating miRNA panels have failed independent validation, and a salivary miRNA signature still needs independent, lower-prevalence validation. Radiomics and AI remain investigational pending external validation, calibration, and demonstrated clinical utility. Non-invasive diagnosis is best framed not as one replacement test but as a multimodal, staged pathway in which each tool is used according to how far its evidence has progressed, which shortens diagnostic delay, targets specialist care, and interprets a negative scan safely.

title: Maternal genitourinary tract infections and spontaneous preterm labor: A narrative review of pathogens, pathways, and prevention.
abstract: Preterm birth is the leading cause of death among children aged under 5 years of age worldwide. Maternal genitourinary tract infections (GUTIs) are among the few modifiable risk factors for spontaneous preterm labor (sPTL), yet the gap between association and effective intervention remains unresolved. This narrative review consolidates recent evidence on GUTIs and sPTL, integrating pathogens, ascending and hematogenous pathways, and prevention. MEDLINE, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Scopus were searched (January 2000-January 2026); evidence was synthesized narratively and stratified by preterm-birth subtype where possible. Pooled estimates showed increased odds of preterm birth with urinary tract infection (odds ratio [OR] 1.92, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.62-2.27), asymptomatic bacteriuria (ASB; OR 1.62, 95% CI 1.30-2.01), bacterial vaginosis (OR 1.79, 95% CI 1.32-2.43), Ureaplasma colonization (OR 2.76, 95% CI 1.63-4.68), Trichomonas vaginalis (relative risk 1.42, 95% CI 1.15-1.75), and Chlamydia trachomatis (OR 1.57, 95% CI 1.11-2.22). A 2026 Swedish register cohort (n = 684 595) demonstrates that the hazard for preterm birth after urinary tract infection (UTI) diagnosis is highest in the first 6 days and declines with advancing gestation (adjusted hazard ratios 18.5, 13.5, and 6.7 at 22-27, 28-31, and 32-36 weeks). Gene-environment analyses further indicate that preterm birth subtypes differ in susceptibility to UTI versus vaginal infection. Antibiotic treatment of ASB reduces pyelonephritis (RR 0.24), but its effect on preterm birth in unselected populations is uncertain. Ascending infection drives decidual cytokine release and premature myometrial activation; amniotic-fluid sludge on transvaginal ultrasound is an accessible marker of subclinical intra-amniotic infection. Targeted screening, evidence-based antibiotic selection, and antimicrobial stewardship remain the practical priorities.

title: Prostatic Adenosquamous Carcinoma With a Minute Squamous Component in the Initial Biopsy and Early Liver Metastasis: A Case Report.
abstract: Introduction We report a case of de novo prostatic adenosquamous carcinoma with a minute squamous component in the initial biopsy and early liver metastasis despite a marked prostate-specific antigen response. Case presentation A 72-year-old man was diagnosed with locally advanced prostate cancer with nodal and multiple bone metastases. Prostate biopsy initially showed adenocarcinoma with a Gleason score of 4 + 5. After leuprolide and abiraterone plus radiotherapy, prostate-specific antigen decreased from 13.0 to 0.22 ng/mL; however, a liver metastasis developed. Re-evaluation of the prostate biopsy revealed minute squamous differentiation, and liver biopsy showed metastatic squamous cell carcinoma. Immunohistochemistry showed retained MLH1 and PMS2 expression with loss of MSH2 and MSH6 in both specimens. Genomic profiling showed microsatellite instability-high status. Conclusion Repeat biopsy and molecular-pathological reassessment may be important when radiographic progression is discordant with prostate-specific antigen kinetics.

title: Leiomyosarcoma of the Renal Vein That Enlarged Laterally While Preserving the Structure of the Renal Vein Lumen.
abstract: Introduction Primary renal vein leiomyosarcoma is an extremely rare disease and the tumor often infiltrates the vessel wall. We report a case of primary renal vein leiomyosarcoma that enlarged while preserving the structure of the renal vein lumen. Case presentation A 64-year-old woman underwent a computed tomography scan, which revealed a left renal hilar mass. Extra-gastrointestinal stromal tumor, leiomyosarcoma, and inflammatory myofibroblastic tumor remained in the differential diagnoses based on blood, urine, and imaging test findings. The tumor, left renal vein, kidney, and adrenal gland were resected. Hematoxylin-eosin staining revealed a tumor arising from the renal vein wall and proliferating outward beyond the vessel. The diagnosis was primary renal vein leiomyosarcoma. Conclusion When a well-defined solid tumor adjacent to the renal vein is identified, leiomyosarcoma should be considered in the differential diagnosis, and complete resection of the tumor should be pursued.

title: Primary Pure Yolk Sac Tumor of the Urinary Bladder: A Case Report.
abstract: Introduction Yolk sac tumors are malignant germ cell tumors that typically arise in the gonads. Although extragonadal cases have been reported, primary involvement of the urinary tract is extremely rare. Case presentation A 67-year-old man presented with gross hematuria. Cystoscopy and contrast-enhanced computed tomography revealed a 6-cm bladder mass. Transurethral resection of the bladder tumor was performed. Histopathological and immunohistochemical findings (alpha-fetoprotein, glypican-3, and Sal-like protein 4 positivity) were consistent with a yolk sac tumor without a urothelial carcinoma component. Additional examinations revealed no primary lesions elsewhere, leading to the diagnosis of a primary bladder yolk sac tumor. The patient received four cycles of etoposide and cisplatin chemotherapy and has remained recurrence-free for 2 years. Conclusions Patients with primary bladder yolk sac tumors, although rare, may achieve favorable outcomes with combined surgical resection and chemotherapy.

title: Photoacoustic Microscopy: Technological Advances, Biomedical Applications, and Future Perspectives.
abstract: Photoacoustic microscopy (PAM) is a powerful subbranch of photoacoustic imaging that achieves microscale spatial resolution and subcellular-level visualization by exploiting endogenous optical contrast, cross-scale capacity, and multiparametric functional readouts. Despite these strengths, clinical translation of PAM is impeded by technical bottlenecks in scanning speed, optical-acoustic coupling, and image reconstruction. This narrative review synthesizes recent engineering breakthroughs that are overcoming these limitations, including advanced scanning architectures, fiber laser sources, high-sensitivity transducers (e.g., CMUTs and transparent ultrasonic detectors), and deep learning-assisted reconstruction algorithms such as attention-based U-Nets and generative adversarial networks. We further highlight representative biomedical applications across dermatology, cerebrovascular hemodynamics, ophthalmology, and gastrointestinal endoscopy, illustrating PAM's versatile diagnostic potential. Finally, we discuss persistent challenges, such as miniaturization, depth penetration, and regulatory hurdles, and propose translational strategies to accelerate PAM's evolution from a laboratory research tool to a mainstream precision medicine imaging modality.

title: A Novel Application of the Volumetric Absorptive Micro Sampling Strategy to Quantify Dexmedetomidine in Capillary Blood Using an LC-MS/MS Method.
abstract: Background Pain control in neonates is crucial as inadequate management may impair neuronal development. Dexmedetomidine (DEX), an alpha2 agonist, is approved for intravenous use in ventilated neonates. While intranasal DEX is off-label in neonates and children, studies show its efficacy for magnetic resonance imaging sedation. Limited pharmacokinetic data exist for intranasal DEX in pre-term infants and neonates. This study aimed to develop an analytical method for DEX quantification in blood samples (20 μL) of complex patients collected with microsampling technique to enable future pharmacokinetic studies. Methods A liquid-liquid extraction from blood absorbed in microsampling devices (MITRA) and an LC-MS/MS method were developed and validated following EMA/FDA guidelines. The method's suitability was verified by comparing results from nine paediatric blood samples collected in EDTA tubes or using MITRA devices. Results All results obtained for selectivity (no interference at R T of DEX), sensitivity (DEX LLOQ = 0.025 ng/mL), linearity (R 2 > 0.99), intra and inter-day repeatability (CV % 1.8-11.8), stability, and hematocrit effect met the acceptance criteria for bioanalytical method validation. Compared with plasma samples, the proposed method showed good consistency in detecting DEX in MITRA samples. Conclusion The MITRA microsampling tools reduce the amount of blood needed and the risks of anemisation for neonates hospitalised and simplifies procedures, allowing a reduction of the staff involved in the routine. The analytical and clinical validation of the method demonstrated its suitability to quantify DEX in a range of concentrations potentially useful for pharmacokinetic studies in paediatric patients for approval use and drug monitoring.

title: Integrated Assessment of Sarcopenia in Patients with Gastric Cancer Using Deep Learning and Radiomics.
abstract: Background Sarcopenia is a common condition in patients with gastric cancer that is associated with poor survival and adverse clinical outcomes. Conventional diagnostic approaches are time-consuming, limiting large-scale clinical implementation. This study aimed to develop and validate a multimodal model that integrates clinical variables, radiomics features and deep learning features. Methods A total of 1067 patients with gastric cancer from two medical centres were included. The diagnosis of sarcopenia required low grip strength and a low skeletal muscle index, whereas severe sarcopenia additionally required low gait speed. Radiomics features were extracted from computed tomography images at the third lumbar vertebral level to construct radiomics models. The 2D and 2.5D deep learning models were developed using the ResNet50 architecture. A transformer-based multimodal model integrating clinical variables, radiomics features and 2.5D deep learning features was developed and termed the sarcopenia model, while an XGBoost fusion model integrating the same three modalities was constructed as a comparator. Model performance was evaluated in the training, validation and external test sets using receiver operating characteristic and decision curve analyses. Results Among the 1067 patients, 782 (73.3%) were male and 285 (26.7%) were female, with no significant difference in gender distribution across the training, validation and external test sets (p = 0.34). Kaplan-Meier survival analysis demonstrated that the overall survival of patients with sarcopenia was significantly worse than that of patients without sarcopenia (p < 0.05). Among single-modality models, the radiomics model achieved AUCs of 0.85 and 0.80 in the validation and external test sets, respectively. The 2.5D deep learning model outperformed the 2D model, yielding AUCs of 0.81 and 0.83 in the validation and external test sets. The XGBoost model achieved AUCs of 0.85 and 0.86 in the validation and external test sets, respectively. In the sarcopenia model, the AUCs for identifying sarcopenia were 0.95, 0.87 and 0.89 in the training, validation and external test sets, respectively, while those for identifying severe sarcopenia were 0.93, 0.85 and 0.84. Conclusions The sarcopenia model integrating clinical variables, radiomics features and deep learning features enables the accurate identification of sarcopenia and severe sarcopenia in patients with gastric cancer and may support clinical screening and risk stratification.

title: Appendicular Skeletal Muscle Mass and Sarcopenia as Prognostic Markers in Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis.
abstract: Background Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is characterized by progressive muscle wasting and functional decline. Prognostic assessment in clinical practice relies largely on functional scales and traditional anthropometric measures. The prognostic relevance of muscle mass, muscle strength and sarcopenia in ALS remains incompletely defined. This study evaluated the prognostic value of muscle mass, muscle function and sarcopenia in relation to mortality in patients with ALS. Methods A prospective observational cohort study was conducted at the ALS Multidisciplinary Unit (UMELA), San Cecilio University Hospital in Granada. Sarcopenia was defined according to the European Working Group of Sarcopenia in Older People 2 (EWGSOP2) and malnutrition using the Global Leadership Initiative on Malnutrition (GLIM) criteria. Muscle status was assessed using bioelectrical impedance vector analysis (BIVA)-derived parameters, muscle ultrasound, handgrip strength (HGS) and physical performance (SPPB). Differences between survivors and nonsurvivors were analysed and logistic regression explored potential predictors of mortality. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were constructed for significant predictors. Survival was analysed using the Kaplan-Meier and Cox proportional hazards regression. Results A total of 42 patients with ALS were included (mean age 66.1 ± 10.3 years, and 15 (36%) were female). During follow-up (mean survival 21.1 ± 10.5 months), 45% died. Survivors showed higher appendicular skeletal muscle mass index (ASMI) (6.94 ± 0.91 vs. 5.80 ± 0.98 kg/m 2 , p = 0.001), body cellular mass index (BCMI) (8.92 ± 1.59 vs. 7.64 ± 1.87 kg/m 2 , p = 0.034) and HGS (25.45 ± 11.11 vs. 17.67 ± 8.83 kg, p = 0.032), while BMI did not differ (p = 0.540). Sarcopenia was more prevalent in nonsurvivors (27.8% vs. 4.8%, p = 0.047). In multivariable analysis, ASMI remained associated with mortality after adjustment for age, onset type and ALSFRS-R (OR 0.33, 95% CI 0.11-0.81, p = 0.026), but this association was not statistically significant in the fully adjusted model including disease duration (p = 0.093). ASMI showed the highest discriminative ability (AUC 0.81), compared to BCMI (AUC 0.70) and HGS (AUC 0.71). ROC-derived cut-offs (ASMI 6.74 kg/m 2 ; BCMI 7.2 kg/m 2 ; HGS 21 kg) stratified survival. Higher ASMI (HR 7.53, p = 0.008), BCMI (HR 4.18, p = 0.005) and HGS (HR 4.02, p = 0.019) were associated with longer survival, whereas sarcopenia increased mortality risk (HR 15.53, p < 0.001). Conclusions Beyond BMI, skeletal muscle mass-particularly ASMI-was associated with survival in ALS. Sarcopenia identifies a subgroup of patients at particularly high risk of death. Sarcopenia assessment may improve prognostic stratification and support clinical management in ALS.

Muscle status was assessed using bioelectrical impedance vector analysis (BIVA)-derived parameters, muscle ultrasound, handgrip strength (HGS) and physical performance (SPPB). Differences between survivors and nonsurvivors were analysed and logistic regression explored potential predictors of mortality. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were constructed for significant predictors. Survival was analysed using the Kaplan-Meier and Cox proportional hazards regression.

Results

A total of 42 patients with ALS were included (mean age 66.1 ± 10.3 years, and 15 (36%) were female). During follow-up (mean survival 21.1 ± 10.5 months), 45% died. Survivors showed higher appendicular skeletal muscle mass index (ASMI) (6.94 ± 0.91 vs. 5.80 ± 0.98 kg/m2, p = 0.001), body cellular mass index (BCMI) (8.92 ± 1.59 vs. 7.64 ± 1.87 kg/m2, p = 0.034) and HGS (25.45 ± 11.11 vs. 17.67 ± 8.83 kg, p = 0.032), while BMI did not differ (p = 0.540). Sarcopenia was more prevalent in nonsurvivors (27.8% vs. 4.8%, p = 0.047). In multivariable analysis, ASMI remained associated with mortality after adjustment for age, onset type and ALSFRS-R (OR 0.33, 95% CI 0.11-0.81, p = 0.026), but this association was not statistically significant in the fully adjusted model including disease duration (p = 0.093). ASMI showed the highest discriminative ability (AUC 0.81), compared to BCMI (AUC 0.70) and HGS (AUC 0.71). ROC-derived cut-offs (ASMI 6.74 kg/m2; BCMI 7.2 kg/m2; HGS 21 kg) stratified survival. Higher ASMI (HR 7.53, p = 0.008), BCMI (HR 4.18, p = 0.005) and HGS (HR 4.02, p = 0.019) were associated with longer survival, whereas sarcopenia increased mortality risk (HR 15.53, p < 0.001).

Conclusions

Beyond BMI, skeletal muscle mass-particularly ASMI-was associated with survival in ALS. Sarcopenia identifies a subgroup of patients at particularly high risk of death. Sarcopenia assessment may improve prognostic stratification and support clinical management in ALS.

title: Quantitative Muscle MRI Fat Fraction as a Biomarker of Disease Severity in Mitochondrial Myopathies.
abstract: Background Quantitative muscle MRI is increasingly used to assess structural muscle damage in inherited myopathies, but its application in primary mitochondrial myopathies (PMM) has not been systematically evaluated in large cohorts. Because PMM are clinically and genetically heterogeneous, objective imaging biomarkers are needed to quantify skeletal-muscle involvement and define meaningful subgroups. We assessed whether MRI-derived proton density fat fraction (PDFF) captures genotype- and phenotype-specific patterns of fatty replacement and reflects disease severity using motor function outcomes and circulating biomarkers. Methods We performed a cross-sectional analysis of 49 adults with genetically confirmed PMM enrolled in a prospective natural history study. Participants underwent standardised lower-limb MRI, including T1-weighted sequences and mDIXON-QUANT fat fraction imaging. Muscle involvement was assessed semi-quantitatively with the modified Mercuri scale and quantitatively by PDFF measurement in selected pelvic girdle and thigh muscles. A total fat fraction score (FF sum) was calculated. PDFF was compared across genotypes and phenotypes and against MRC score, NSAA, 6-min walk test, 100-m run test, CK, serum creatinine, GDF15 and disease duration. Results Mean age at onset was 26.3 ± 15.1 years, mean age at MRI was 50.0 ± 12.3 years, and median disease duration was 23 years (IQR 15-31). Genetic diagnoses included mtDNA variants in 29 patients (59.1%; single large-scale deletions, n = 19; point mutations, n = 10), nuclear variants in POLG (n = 8), TK2 (n = 8) and TWNK (n = 4). Phenotypes were exercise intolerance without overt weakness (n = 7), isolated progressive external ophthalmoplegia (PEO; n = 16), PEO-plus (n = 16) and progressive myopathy (n = 8). Highest median PDFF values were observed in tensor fasciae latae (31%), gluteus maximus (30%), sartorius (25%) and gracilis (20%). FF sum correlated with MRC score (r = -0.567, p < 0.0001), NSAA (r = -0.731, p < 0.0001), 100-m run test time (r = 0.629, p < 0.0001), 6-min walk distance (r = -0.311, p = 0.0476) and serum creatinine (r = -0.715, p < 0.0001), but not with CK or GDF15. TK2 deficiency showed the highest fat replacement, particularly in gluteus maximus and gracilis (p < 0.001). Progressive myopathy showed greater fatty replacement than other phenotypes (p < 0.001), while exercise intolerance showed higher fat fraction than isolated PEO (p = 0.033). Conclusions Quantitative muscle MRI provides objective and clinically meaningful measures of muscle involvement in PMM. MRI-derived fat fraction reflects disease severity, discriminates between genotypes and phenotypes, and detects subclinical muscle damage. These cross-sectional findings support PDFF as a candidate imaging biomarker for patient stratification and disease characterisation; prospective longitudinal studies will be required to establish its sensitivity to change and its validity as an outcome measure for therapeutic trials.

title: Metastatic Bone Disease Is Associated With Longitudinal Muscle Loss and Reduced Survival in Kidney Cancer.
abstract: Background Cachexia is a multifactorial muscle wasting syndrome and is responsible for 20%-40% of cancer-related deaths, yet no FDA-approved therapies exist. Preclinical studies suggest that metastatic bone disease may contribute to muscle wasting, but this relationship has not been evaluated in clinical populations. This study evaluated whether metastatic bone disease at diagnosis is associated with longitudinal skeletal muscle loss and whether metastatic bone disease and longitudinal skeletal muscle loss are associated with overall survival in patients with kidney cancer. Methods A total of 293 patients (66.9% male, 33.1% female, median age 60 years) were retrospectively identified with either localised kidney cancer, extraosseous metastatic disease, or osseous metastatic disease at diagnosis. Clinical and demographic variables and treatments were recorded. Body composition was quantified over time for a subset by body mass index (BMI) (N = 221) and CT analysis at the L3 vertebral level (N = 99). Longitudinal changes were analysed using linear regression, and overall survival was assessed with Kaplan-Meier and multivariable Cox proportional hazards models. Results Patients with osseous metastatic disease had a reduction in BMI over time compared with those with localised or extraosseous metastatic disease (median of -3.6% per year, compared with +0.7% and -2.6% respectively, p < 0.01). Skeletal muscle loss was greatest for those with osseous metastasis (-7.5% per year, compared with -0.8% and -1.2% respectively, p < 0.01). Multivariable linear regression demonstrated osseous metastasis at diagnosis was strongly associated with muscle loss (β coefficient of -20.9 [95% confidence interval (CI): -35.56 to -6.27]). In multivariable Cox regression analysis, osseous metastasis at diagnosis was associated with an increased risk of death (HR 15.8; 95% CI: 2.00 to 124.95; p < 0.01), as was longitudinal skeletal muscle loss (HR 1.02 for each 1% loss per year; 95% CI: 1.01 to 1.04; p < 0.01). Conclusions This study provides the first clinical evidence that metastatic bone disease is strongly associated with skeletal muscle loss and reduced survival in kidney cancer patients. These findings extend prior preclinical observations into the clinical setting and support further investigation into the possibility that tumour-bone-muscle interactions drive systemic muscle wasting. Importantly, the observation that severe muscle loss is strongly associated with mortality in kidney cancer highlights the need to consider cachexia as a modifiable determinant of outcomes, not just a byproduct of advanced disease.

title: Clinical and Sonographic Features of Neonatal Ovarian Cysts With Autoamputation.
abstract: Purpose Autoamputation is a rare but severe complication of neonatal ovarian cysts. This case series describes the clinical, sonographic, and pathological characteristics of neonatal ovarian cysts that progressed to autoamputation, compared with those that did not, based on a retrospective review of 19 cysts. We aim to help clinicians suspect autoamputation when managing complex neonatal ovarian cysts. Methods Medical records of 18 neonates (19 ovarian cysts) treated at two medical centers between January 2012 and December 2023 were reviewed. All cysts appeared complex on postnatal ultrasonography. We documented prenatal and postnatal sonographic features (cyst size, solid components, septations, fluid-debris levels, calcification), timing of examinations, intraoperative findings (adhesions, autoamputation), and pathology results. Descriptive statistics and exploratory comparisons between autoamputation (n = 9 cysts) and non-autoamputation (n = 10 cysts) groups were performed, without claims of predictive modeling. Results Of the 19 complex ovarian cysts, 9 (47.3%) were confirmed autoamputated at surgery. The autoamputation group showed a longer median interval from first complex features to surgery (68 vs. 21.5 days) and an older age at last postnatal ultrasound (11 vs. 1 days). Intra-abdominal adhesions were observed in 66.7% of autoamputation cases versus 10% of non-autoamputation cases. Follicles were absent in all autoamputated cysts on pathology but present in 90% of non-autoamputated cysts. Sonographic findings evolved over time: fluid-debris levels became the predominant feature with increasing duration, while calcification appeared late (22.2% in the autoamputation group). Conclusion Autoamputation of neonatal ovarian cysts was associated with a longer interval from first complex features to surgery, absence of follicles on pathology, and frequent intra-abdominal adhesions. Sonographic features evolved over time, with fluid-debris levels becoming common and calcification appearing late but with poor sonographic sensitivity. These observations may help clinicians better understand the evolution of complex neonatal ovarian cysts associated with autoamputation; however, the diagnostic and predictive value of these findings requires further validation.

title: Review of Ultrasound Diagnosis of Ichthyosis in Fetuses.
abstract: Congenital ichthyoses are inherited disorders in which the outer layer of the skin forms abnormally. Prenatal ultrasound can show a recognizable pattern in some affected fetuses, but most published evidence comes from case reports and small case series. This narrative review summarizes sonographic findings that have been reported, when they became visible, and how they should be interpreted in clinical practice. The strongest imaging literature concerns harlequin ichthyosis. Reported findings include ectropion, eclabium or persistent mouth opening, a flattened nasal contour, fixed flexion of the hands or feet, an abnormal skin surface, echogenic amniotic fluid, and polyhydramnios. However, these findings are not specific and may appear only in the second half of pregnancy. Therefore, an earlier normal scan does not exclude disease. Evidence for other congenital ichthyoses is more limited. A genotype-confirmed TGM1-related case showed facial findings similar to harlequin ichthyosis, whereas ichthyosis prematurity syndrome has a late-gestation pattern described in a small series. By contrast, X-linked ichthyosis is more often suspected from maternal serum or genetic findings than from a structural fetal ultrasound pattern. Three-dimensional ultrasound can improve display of surface anatomy when two-dimensional findings are suspicious, but its diagnostic accuracy has not been established. Fetal magnetic resonance imaging has only an adjunctive role. Overall, ultrasound is best used to recognize a phenotype, guide further assessment, and prompt genetic testing rather than to provide a stand-alone molecular diagnosis.

title: Ultrasound Features of Ossifying Renal Tumor of Infancy: A Report of Four Cases.
abstract: Ossifying renal tumor of infancy (ORTI) is an extremely rare benign renal tumor that typically presents with painless gross hematuria in infants. We describe the ultrasound features of four pathologically confirmed cases. All lesions were well-defined, hyperechoic masses located near a renal pole, protruding into the collecting system while preserving the renal contour. Calcification with posterior acoustic shadowing was present in every case. In the two cases with stored color Doppler images, internal signals were sparse. title: A Pain in the Buttocks: Practice Article for Sonographically Imaging the Quadratus Femoris and Ischiofemoral Impingement.
abstract: Ischiofemoral impingement (IFI) results in buttock, hip, and groin pain which can radiate down the leg. Clinical diagnosis of IFI is challenging due to the overlap of other syndrome symptoms, which can delay appropriate management. Hip external rotation reduces the ischiofemoral and quadratus femoris (QF) spaces, compressing the QF muscle between the ischial tuberosity and the lesser trochanter. Ultrasound imaging can demonstrate dynamic entrapment of the QF, including assessment of symptom provocation and concurrently identify injury or irritation of nearby structures including the peri-QF fat, sciatic nerve, and proximal hamstring tendons.

title: Longitudinal Ultrasonographic Appearance of an Atypical Tendinous Variant of Popliteal Artery Entrapment Syndrome in an Adolescent.
abstract: A 15-year-old boy presented with left fifth-toe ulceration, claudication, and rest pain. Computed tomography angiography demonstrated proximal-to-mid popliteal artery occlusion. Duplex ultrasonography revealed thrombotic occlusion and a slender tendon crossing the artery, which appeared more conspicuous longitudinally than transversely. Magnetic resonance imaging showed apparent continuity with the main tendon of the medial head of the gastrocnemius, supporting an atypical variant of popliteal artery entrapment syndrome. Surgery was declined. At 3 months, the ulcer had healed, and symptoms improved during medical therapy, although perfusion indices remained abnormal. Longitudinal ultrasonography may facilitate delineation of slender compressive tendons.

title: Isolated Hoarseness as the Initial Presentation of a Rare Primary Anterior Mediastinal Large-Cell Neuroendocrine Carcinoma: Multimodal Ultrasound Features-A Case Report.
abstract: Primary large-cell neuroendocrine carcinoma (LCNEC) of the anterior-superior mediastinum is an exceedingly rare and aggressive malignancy. We report a case in a 38-year-old man who presented with isolated hoarseness as the only initial symptom, an uncommon clinical presentation that has rarely been reported in the literature. Multimodal ultrasound showed a hypoechoic mass with an inverted triangular morphology, markedly increased stiffness on elastography, and a "fast-in and fast-out" enhancement pattern on contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS). The patient received platinum-based chemotherapy with concurrent thoracic radiotherapy followed by maintenance immunotherapy and remained alive with stable disease/partial response at the last follow-up. This report is the first to define and summarize the tumor's multimodal ultrasound findings, aiming to improve early recognition of this rare entity and to provide a useful imaging clue for clinical practice.

title: Integrated Bedside Hemodynamic Assessment and Monitoring of Venous Congestion With Venous Excess Ultrasound (VExUS): A Narrative Review.
abstract: This review evaluates the venous excess ultrasound (VExUS) score as a bedside tool for quantifying systemic venous congestion and predicting congestive end-organ injury, particularly acute kidney injury (AKI). By assessing flow patterns in the hepatic, portal, and renal veins alongside inferior vena cava (IVC) size, VExUS enables serial monitoring of congestion trajectories. While highly prognostic in heart failure, its predictive performance varies in more heterogeneous populations. Ultimately, integrating VExUS with cardiac output indices may help clinicians identify specific hemodynamic phenotypes, guiding targeted, individualized therapeutic strategies.

title: Contrast-Enhanced Ultrasound in the Diagnosis of Parotid Gland Castleman Disease in a Child.
abstract: Castleman disease is a rare lymphoproliferative disorder that infrequently involves the parotid gland. We report a 16-year-old girl with a 3-year history of slowly progressive, painless right cheek swelling. CT and MRI showed an avidly enhancing, markedly T2-hyperintense parotid lesion, suggesting a vascular malformation; fine-needle aspiration yielded reactive lymphoid tissue. Contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) demonstrated rapid, intense, homogeneous enhancement, confirming a hypervascular solid mass rather than a vascular malformation and raising suspicion for Castleman disease. Superficial parotidectomy confirmed unicentric hyaline-vascular Castleman disease. CEUS aided differentiation of a hypervascular solid lesion from a vascular malformation and narrowed the differential.
