title: Preoperative prevalence and risk factors for thromboembolic events following tibial plateau fractures: a retrospective analysis of an underestimated risk.
abstract: Background Tibial plateau fractures (TPF) are complex intra-articular injuries carrying a high risk of deep vein thrombosis (DVT), muscular vein thrombosis (MVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE). Preoperative thrombosis is frequently clinically silent yet may cause serious complications, whereas its detection delays definitive surgery. This study assessed the prevalence and risk factors of preoperative venous thromboembolic events (VTE) in surgically treated TPF before and after implementation of routine duplex ultrasound screening. Methods In this retrospective single-centre study at a level 1 trauma centre, all adult patients surgically treated for traumatic TPF (AO 41B/C) between January 2015 and August 2025 were reviewed (547 patients, 554 fractures). Until August 2020 duplex ultrasound (DUS) was performed only on clinical suspicion; from August 2020 onward routine preoperative DUS was progressively implemented. VTE were confirmed by DUS or CT angiography. Prevalences are reported per fracture and patient characteristics per patient; regression analyses were performed at fracture level, except for the patient-related model. Results With DUS restricted to clinical suspicion (cohort A; 246 fractures), the detected prevalence of preoperative VTE was 3.7% (95% CI 1.9-6.8) and that of DVT 2.4% (1.1-5.2). Under routine screening (cohort B; 205 screened fractures) it was 20.0% (15.1-26.0) and 17.1% (12.5-22.8), respectively, 82.9% of DVT being distal. Given the different diagnostic strategies, this reflects the higher diagnostic yield of screening rather than a true increase in VTE. In cohort B, 28 of 41 VTE (68.3%) and 24 of 35 DVT (68.6%) were clinically silent. Two patients had in-hospital cardiac arrest from PE: one died from a DVT undetected before screening was introduced, the other had an asymptomatic DVT identified by screening. VTE was independently associated with pre-existing therapeutic anticoagulation (adjusted OR 2.96, 95% CI 1.10-7.98) and with the duration of external fixation (adjusted OR 1.11 per day, 1.02-1.20). High-grade closed soft-tissue injury (adjusted OR 2.41, 1.07-5.45), polytrauma (adjusted OR 2.24, 1.07-4.68) and initial external fixation (univariable OR 3.60, 1.76-7.35) were also associated with VTE, but none remained significant after accounting for fixation duration (adjusted OR 1.42, 0.52-3.89; 1.96, 0.76-5.05; 0.62, 0.12-3.27), i.e. risk was driven by time in the fixator rather than by external fixation as such. Conclusions Surgically treated TPF carry a substantial burden of preoperative VTE, and routine DUS reveals a high proportion of clinically silent thrombosis that would otherwise remain undetected. Severe closed soft-tissue injury, pre-existing therapeutic anticoagulation and, above all, the duration of external fixation may help to identify patients at increased risk. As two diagnostic rather than two treatment strategies were compared, the study cannot determine whether screening improves outcomes or reduces PE; prospective evaluation of structured screening and risk-adapted thromboprophylaxis is warranted.

title: [Anti-amyloid antibodies against Alzheimer's disease : Lecanemab and donanemab in practice-Clinical importance, patient selection and safety management].
abstract: Lecanemab and donanemab are the first disease-modifying therapies for early Alzheimer's disease. These humanized IgG1 antibodies promote the clearance of aggregated amyloid-beta peptides and, in the pivotal CLARITY AD and TRAILBLAZER-ALZ 2 trials, significantly delayed cognitive and functional decline, with an approximately 30% relative risk reduction for the clinical stage progression; however, the clinical meaningfulness remains contested: critics point to the small between-group difference in relation to the total score. This is weighed against the first disease-modifying effect and the first pharmacotherapy for mild cognitive impairment due to Alzheimer's disease. A prerequisite is the biological diagnosis: the reference standard is cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and amyloid positron emission tomography (PET), potentially complemented in the future by blood biomarkers such as plasma p‑Tau217. Amyloid-related imaging abnormalities (ARIA) are the key adverse event, manageable through patient selection, ApoE-ε4 genotyping and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) monitoring. The indications and follow-up belong in specialized centers.

title: [Contrast agent strategies in elective oncological imaging].
abstract: Computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) are central to staging, treatment planning and response assessment in oncology. For many tumor entities, clinical guidelines specify the recommended imaging frequency and appropriate modality; however, the practical implementation, including the applied imaging protocols, varies in clinical routine. Intravenous contrast agents are indispensable in oncological imaging for a variety of specific clinical questions, particularly for the detection and characterization of intraparenchymal lesions. In addition to the general indications for contrast administration, the selection of the optimal contrast phase for subsequent imaging is crucial. This article outlines the fundamentals of iodine-based and gadolinium-based contrast agents, their pharmacokinetics and safety aspects that should be considered in the context of a risk-benefit assessment for their use in oncological imaging. Furthermore, typical contrast phases and imaging protocols are presented as representative examples. Future developments in this field include spectral imaging and photon-counting CT, quantitative imaging and artificial intelligence (AI)-based methods as well as contrast agent-free functional MRI techniques. All of these approaches aim to achieve more precise tissue characterization, a potential reduction of radiation dose and/or contrast agent use as well as automated optimization of image acquisition and interpretation and are also discussed in this article.

title: [Enteral contrast agents-When, what and how?]
abstract: Background Administration of enteral contrast media (CM) in abdominal computed tomography (CT) is handled inconsistently across Germany. Objective To present the current recommendations on administration of enteral contrast agents along the guiding questions of when, what and how and to translate them into radiological practice. Material and methods Synthesis of indication-based recommendations, CM classes and their technical properties and the practical execution of both routes of administration, based on the recommendations of the German Röntgen Society (DRG), current guidelines, published evidence and institutional practice. Results Positive oral CMs are obsolete for most abdominal indications, including acute abdomen, ileus and trauma, and are contraindicated when gastrointestinal bleeding or ischemia is suspected. In cases of suspected perforation, routine oral contrast agents should be omitted and barium sulphate is contraindicated, whereas water-soluble iodinated agents remain an option when a leak has to be specifically demonstrated. Furthermore, enteral contrasting with neutral oral CM remains useful for upper gastrointestinal tumor staging and enterography (preferably magnetic resonance enterography). Conclusion An indication-appropriate, guideline-based enteral contrast agent administration reduces unnecessary burden without compromising diagnostic accuracy and should be embedded in standardized workflows.

title: [Hepatic postinterventional imaging : Modality selection, assessment of therapeutic response, recognition, and radiological management of typical complications].
abstract: Background Postprocedural imaging following hepatic interventions is essential for monitoring treatment success and detecting complications. Objective To provide an overview of imaging follow-up after hepatic interventions (transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt [TIPS], percutaneous transhepatic cholangiography and drainage [PTCD], transarterial chemoembolization [TACE], ablation, selective internal radiotherapy [SIRT]), focusing on the selection of imaging modalities, the assessment of treatment success, and the recognition and radiological management of complications. Materials and methods Narrative review based on the current literature of hepatic radiological interventions. Results The procedure determines the choice of imaging modality. Following TIPS, functional monitoring is primarily performed using duplex ultrasound. PTCD follow-up focuses on drainage placement and bleeding complications. Following TACE and ablation, immediate hypoperfusion of the lesions is to be expected, whereas a temporary increase in size and peripheral enhancement may occur. Following SIRT, a delayed onset of the treatment effect, as detectable by imaging morphology, is characteristic. Bleeding, abscess formation, fistulas, stent occlusions or malfunctions, and tumor recurrences can be treated further using interventional radiology. Conclusion Knowledge of typical postprocedural imaging findings, as well as common complications and options for radiological treatment of complications, is crucial.

title: Dual-respiratory-phase low-dose quantitative CT for assessing COPD severity.
abstract: Objective To evaluate the ability of quantitative parameters derived from low-dose dual-respiratory-phase CT to differentiate the severity of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). Materials and methods We enrolled 100 COPD patients between October 2023 and October 2024. Inspiratory CT scans were performed using a standard-dose protocol, and expiratory scans were performed using a low-dose protocol. Images were reconstructed with 60% adaptive statistical iterative reconstruction (ASIR). Dual-respiratory-phase image registration was performed on a dedicated "Digital Lung" platform to quantify the following parameters: end-expiratory lung volume (LV EX ), end-inspiratory lung volume (LV IN ), mean lung density at end-inspiration (MLD IN ), mean lung density at end-expiration (MLD EX ), and the mean density ratio (MLD EX/IN ). The percentages of low-attenuation areas (LAA-910% and LAA-950%), emphysema (Emph%), and functional small airways disease (fSAD%) were also calculated. Correlations between CT parameters and pulmonary function were assessed. Significant variables were entered into univariate and multivariate logistic regression models, and a combined predictive model was constructed. Model performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis with internal validation by bootstrap resampling. Results Quantitative parameters, including LV EX , LV IN , LAA-950%, LAA-910%, Emph%, and fSAD%, were significantly correlated with pulmonary function indices (FEV 1 %pred and FEV 1 /FVC; all P < 0.01). Among these, LAA-910% and Emph% showed the strongest correlations with FEV 1 %pred (both r = -0.80). In univariate analysis, LAA-910% demonstrated the highest predictive performance (area under the curve [AUC] = 0.887), followed by Emph% (AUC = 0.884). After adjustment for age and smoking status, multivariate logistic regression identified both Emph% (odds ratio [OR] = 1.298, 95% CI: 1.167-1.488, P < 0.001) and fSAD% (OR = 1.111, 95% CI: 1.040-1.205, P = 0.004) as independent predictors of severe COPD (GOLD 3-4 vs. GOLD 1-2). The combined model incorporating fSAD% and Emph% achieved an AUC of 0.926 (95% CI: 0.883-0.974), with a sensitivity of 80.49% and a specificity of 81.36%. Bootstrap internal validation yielded an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.908, confirming good model generalizability. Conclusion Low-dose expiratory CT combined with dual-respiratory-phase quantitative analysis provides reliable imaging biomarkers that correlate strongly with pulmonary function. The predictive model incorporating both fSAD% and Emph% demonstrates excellent diagnostic performance for assessing COPD severity and may serve as a noninvasive adjunct tool for disease stratification.

title: Vaginal Canal Segmentation with nnU-Net Algorithm from MRI Defecography for Biomechanical Analysis.
abstract: Introduction and hypothesis Accurate three-dimensional segmentation of the vaginal canal is essential for patient-specific pelvic floor modeling, biomechanical analysis, and the development of personalized intravaginal devices. However, manual segmentation of magnetic resonance defecography (MRD) images is time-consuming and prone to observer variability. This study aimed to develop and evaluate an automated deep learning pipeline using the nnU-Net framework for vaginal canal segmentation from MRD images. Methods In this retrospective study, 47 women who underwent MRD for symptoms of pelvic floor dysfunction were included. The vaginal canal was manually annotated on three-dimensional T2-weighted MRD volumes using 3D Slicer to generate ground-truth binary masks. A 3D full-resolution nnU-Net model was trained and evaluated using fivefold cross-validation. Segmentation accuracy was assessed using the Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) and intersection over union (IoU). Predicted masks were further processed using hole filling, marching cubes surface reconstruction, and Taubin smoothing to generate three-dimensional meshes and extract vaginal volume and surface area. Results The nnU-Net model achieved high segmentation accuracy, with a mean DSC of 0.9714 and a mean IoU of 0.9675. Automated segmentation of a full 3D MRD volume required < 1 s, compared with approximately 30-45 min for manual segmentation. The mean vaginal volume was 38.74 ± 13.98 cm 3 , and the mean vaginal surface area was 82.31 ± 19.31 cm 2 . Conclusions The nnU-Net framework enables rapid, accurate, and reproducible segmentation of the gel-distended vaginal lumen from MRD images. This automated pipeline may facilitate standardized three-dimensional measurement of the visible vaginal cavity and provide geometry for patient-specific biomechanical modeling.

title: Does 25(OH)D deficiency affect muscle elasticity, physical function, pain, and quality of life? A shear-wave elastography-based cross-sectional study.
abstract: In this cross-sectional study of 80 young adults, 25(OH)D deficiency (< 20 ng/mL) was associated with lower SWE-measured muscle elasticity (FCR, BB, and TA), and reduced fingertip pinch strength. When women and men were evaluated separately, muscle elasticity values were lower in the low 25(OH)D group in both sexes. Muscle elasticity showed strong correlations with 25(OH)D and accurately discriminated deficiency (AUC 0.935-0.957) in this young cohort. Background Vitamin D is a key biological regulator in maintaining bone mineralization and muscle function by regulating calcium and phosphorus metabolism, promoting muscle protein synthesis, and supporting muscle cell growth and differentiation. Aim To assess muscle elasticity using shear-wave elastography (SWE) in young adults with low and adequate 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D] and explore the diagnostic usefulness of SWE in distinguishing 25(OH)D deficiency. Design A cross-sectional study. Setting Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation and Radiology Departments in the Selcuk University Faculty of Medicine Hospital. Population Eighty participants (18-45 years) were included in two groups regarding 25(OH)D levels. Methods Participants with serum 25(OH)D levels( < 20 ng/mL and those with ≥ 20 ng/mL) were classified as Groups I(n = 40) and II(n = 40). Muscle elasticity of flexor carpi radialis (FCR), short head of biceps brachii (BB), and tibialis anterior (TA) was measured using SWE (kPa). Results Group I consisted of 21 women and 19 men, while Group II consisted of 22 women and 18 men. The groups were similar in demographic characteristics, physical activity, and SF-36 scores. FCR-kPa, BB-kPa, and TA-kPa were lower in Group I (p < 0.001). When women and men were evaluated separately, FCR, BB, and TA muscle elasticity values were significantly lower in both sexes in the low 25(OH)D group (all p < 0.001). Fingertip pinch strength was lower in the dominant and non-dominant hands in Group I (p = 0.001; p = 0.023). AUC values for predicting 25(OH)D deficiency were FCR: 0.94 (cut-off 23.5 kPa), BB: 0.957 (26.5 kPa), and TA: 0.935 (23.75 kPa). Serum 25(OH)D showed a strong positive correlation with elasticity measurements (r = 0.870-0.916; p < 0.001). Conclusion Low 25(OH)D levels were found to be associated with lower elasticity values, as measured by SWE, in FCR, BB, and TA muscles in women and men.

title: Association between the frequency of achieving recommended daily step counts and a decline in quantitative ultrasound measurements in premenopausal and postmenopausal women: a 4-year prospective study of the Tohoku Medical Megabank Community-Based Cohort study.
abstract: Achieving 7000 steps/day on ≥3 days/week significantly reduced the risk of decline in quantitative ultrasound measurements in premenopausal women, but not in postmenopausal women. Less frequent achievement (1-2 days/week) showed no significant association in either group. Purpose To examine the association between the frequency of achieving the recommended daily step count (7000 steps/day) and the incidence of a decline in quantitative ultrasound (QUS) measurements among pre- and postmenopausal women. Methods In this prospective cohort study of the Tohoku Medical Megabank Community-Based Cohort, baseline and follow-up surveys were conducted between 2013-2016 and 2017-2021 (mean follow-up: 42.5 months). Participants were 3529 women (1013 premenopausal, 2516 postmenopausal). Daily steps were objectively measured using pedometers. The number of days per week achieving 7000 steps was categorized as Inactive (0 days), Low active (1-2 days), and Active (≥3 days). The outcome was the incidence of a decline in QUS measurements, defined as a QUS T-score ≤-2.5 or a self-reported diagnosis of osteoporosis. Adjusted risk ratio (RR) and 95% confidence interval (CI) were calculated using modified Poisson regression models, with the Inactive group as the reference. Results During follow-up, the outcome occurred in 70 premenopausal and 662 postmenopausal women. In premenopausal women, the Active group had a significantly lower risk of the outcome compared to the Inactive group (RR: 0.478, 95% CI: 0.271 to 0.843). In postmenopausal women, no statistically significant association was observed (RR for the Active group: 0.937, 95% CI: 0.807 to 1.088). Conclusion The findings suggest that the association appeared to differ by menopausal status, achieving 7000 steps/day on ≥3 days/week was associated with a significantly reduced risk of a decline in QUS measurements in premenopausal women. However, for postmenopausal women, walking alone may be an insufficient strategy.

title: A Clinical Primer on Computer Vision.
abstract: Computer vision is a rapidly evolving field within computer science that focuses on extracting meaningful information from digital images. In medical imaging, computer vision techniques such as object detection, classification, and segmentation are essential for analysing complex anatomical structures. This primer provides an overview of computer vision concepts and methods, highlighting both traditional approaches and modern machine learning techniques. Landmark detection and shape modelling are also discussed as these are particularly relevant for musculoskeletal imaging. Challenges associated with applying computer vision in clinical practice are examined. This includes considerations such as data limitations, domain shift, and the need for robust validation. Finally, future directions for integrating computer vision into osteoporosis research and clinical workflows are explored, emphasising the importance of explainability, fairness, and adherence to guiding principles for trustworthy clinical tools.

Finally, future directions for integrating computer vision into osteoporosis research and clinical workflows are explored, emphasising the importance of explainability, fairness, and adherence to guiding principles for trustworthy clinical tools.

title: Compartment-specific skeletal involvement in systemic sclerosis characterized by peripheral QCT and serum osteoimmune mediators: a case-control study.
abstract: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is associated with increased bone fragility, yet early, compartment-specific alterations and their osteoimmunological correlates remain incompletely characterized. This study aimed to assess bone status in SSc using dual X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) complemented by peripheral quantitative computed tomography (pQCT), and to evaluate their associations with a targeted osteoimmunological biomarker panel and clinical risk scores. This prospective cross-sectional study included 40 women with SSc (disease duration ≤ 7 years from diagnosis) and 45 non-immune female controls, frequency-matched by age. Bone status was assessed by DXA (lumbar spine, femoral neck) and distal radius pQCT. Serum levels of routine bone and mineral metabolism markers, alongside a targeted panel of osteoimmunological mediators (OPG, OPN, PDGF-BB, ACP5, RANKL, TNF-α, IL-6, IL-1β, DKK-1) using multiplex immunoassay were measured. FRAX scores were calculated to contextualize clinical fracture risk. With broadly comparable DXA-defined bone status, pQCT revealed significantly lower trabecular volumetric bone mineral density (vBMD) in SSc, while total and cortical+subcortical vBMD were comparable. Routine biochemical markers showed substantial overlap between groups, whereas SSc patients exhibited a distinct osteoimmune profile with significantly elevated OPG, ACP5, RANKL, PDGF-BB, IL-6, IL-1β, DKK-1, and RANKL/OPG after FDR correction. Exploratory biomarker-bone associations did not remain significant after correction for multiple testing. In women with relatively early SSc, pQCT identified compartment-specific differences, particularly within the trabecular compartment, despite comparable DXA-defined bone status. A distinct osteoimmunological biomarker profile was also observed in SSc, providing complementary information on disease-related skeletal alterations, while specific biomarker-bone associations require further confirmation.

title: Differentiating pituitary metastases from pituitary neuroendocrine tumors in patients with a history of malignancy: clinical and magnetic resonance imaging features and quantitative morphometric analysis.
abstract: Purpose To compare the clinical and MRI findings of pituitary metastases (PMs) and pituitary neuroendocrine tumors (PitNETs) in patients with a history of malignancy and to assess quantitative morphologic parameters in dumbbell-shaped lesions. Methods Clinical and MRI data from 13 patients with PMs and 31 patients with PitNETs were retrospectively reviewed. For 27 dumbbell-shaped lesions, quantitative linear measurements were performed, and the R value was defined as the ratio of the neck diameter to the combined suprasellar and intrasellar widths. Receiver operating characteristic analysis assessed diagnostic performance. Results Patients with PMs had a shorter symptom-to-detection interval (P = 0.003) and more commonly presented with headache (P = 0.004). Compared with the PitNET group, the PM group showed a higher contrast-enhanced T1-weighted signal intensity ratio (P = 0.035), more frequent pituitary stalk involvement (P = 0.024), less frequent preservation of the posterior pituitary bright spot (P < 0.001), and less frequent sellar enlargement (P = 0.010). In the subgroup with dumbbell-shaped lesions, the PM group had a smaller coronal suprasellar width (P = 0.004), smaller coronal and sagittal neck diameters, and lower coronal and sagittal R values (all P < 0.001). Coronal neck diameter and coronal R value yielded AUCs of 0.986 and 0.971, respectively. Conclusion In patients with a history of malignancy and a newly detected sellar lesion, a shorter symptom-to-detection interval, headache, pituitary stalk involvement, loss of the posterior pituitary bright spot, marked enhancement, and limited sellar enlargement may suggest PM. In dumbbell-shaped lesions, a smaller neck diameter and lower R value may provide supplementary quantitative information for differentiating PMs from PitNETs.

title: Exploring the role of glymphatic system in Alzheimer's disease with insights from MRI-based studies: a systematic review.
abstract: Background The glymphatic constitutes a crucial neurophysiological mechanism for the clearance of interstitial solutes and neurotoxic metabolites from the central nervous system. Dysfunction within this pathway is increasingly implicated in the etiopathogenesis of neurodegenerative diseases, notably Alzheimer's disease (AD). Advanced magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) modalities, such as diffusion tensor image analysis along the perivascular space (DTI-ALPS), have emerged as non-invasive, in vivo approaches quantifying glymphatic transport efficacy and its association with cognitive decline and AD progression. Methods This systematic review was conducted in adherence with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. and systematic literature retrieval was executed across PubMed, Cochrane, and Scopus databases, targeting studies that employed MRI-based metrics to assess glymphatic functionality in the context of AD. Results A total of 35 studies fulfilled the inclusion criteria. AD patients exhibited significantly reduced DTI-ALPS indices, correlating with elevated enlarged perivascular space (ePVS) volumes, neurocognitive deterioration, and cerebral atrophy. Notably ePVSs enlargement emerged as a surrogate marker of glymphatic dysfunction and a predictor of MCI-to-AD conversion. However, amyloid PET correlations exhibited inter-study heterogeneity. Conclusions MRI derived biomarkers, particularly DTI-ALPS index and ePVSs analysis, demonstrate high potential as surrogate indicators of glymphatic impairment in AD. These findings underscore their diagnostic and prognostic value, warranting harmonization of imaging protocols and longitudinal investigations to establish their translational utility in clinical biomarker frameworks. Clinical relevance statement MRI biomarkers of glymphatic dysfunction provide valuable insights into Alzheimer's disease pathophysiology and progression. These imaging markers may enhance early diagnosis, monitor disease progression, and evaluate treatment efficacy in AD.

title: Perivascular spaces as MRI markers associated with radiation necrosis in brain metastases patients: an exploratory study.
abstract: Background and purpose Radiation necrosis (RN) is a significant complication of stereotactic radiotherapy (SRT) for brain metastases. We investigated whether pre-treatment cerebral small vessel disease (cSVD) burden, particularly perivascular spaces (PVSs), is associated with RN risk. Materials and methods This single-center retrospective study included 71 patients treated with fractionated SRT for brain metastases. RN was diagnosed by consensus using multiparametric MRI including DSC perfusion. Pre-treatment cSVD markers were evaluated according to STRIVE criteria, with PVSs graded using Potter's criteria in the basal ganglia (BG), centrum semiovale (CS), and midbrain (MB). Associations with RN were assessed using Firth's penalized logistic regression adjusted for age and sex. Results RN developed in 33 patients (46.5%). Higher PVS grades in the CS were significantly associated with increased RN risk (grade 1: OR 6.35, 95% CI 1.86-21.72, p = 0.003; grade 2: OR 26.26, 95% CI 3.64-189.61, p = 0.001). Associations were also observed for higher PVS burden in the BG and MB, although these rested on small subsets with wide confidence intervals. Other cSVD markers showed no significant associations. Confidence intervals were wide due to sparse data in higher PVS grades. Conclusions This exploratory study suggests a potential association between pre-treatment PVS burden and RN risk. However, sparse data, wide confidence intervals, and the absence of lesion-level dosimetric adjustment limit conclusions. These preliminary findings warrant validation in larger, prospective cohorts with comprehensive dosimetric analysis.

title: A multi-stage multimodal learning model for functional outcomes prediction in acute ischemic stroke.
abstract: Predicting functional outcomes in acute ischemic stroke (AIS) patients after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) remains challenging due to the complex and dynamic nature of disease progression. Existing methods typically rely on single-stage imaging or limited multimodal fusion, failing to fully capture disease progression and cross-modal complementarity. To address this issue, we propose a multimodal deep learning framework that integrates multi-stage imaging and clinical notes for 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS) prediction. The proposed model leverages a shared foundation model with Low-Rank Adaptation to encode pre- and post-treatment images. It further introduces a shared feature extraction module and a stage-specific feature extraction module to disentangle shared and stage-specific representations, enabling effective modeling of disease progression across stages. In addition, a bidirectional cross-attention module is employed to enhance semantic alignment between imaging features and clinical notes. Experiments on multi-stage NCCT and MRI datasets demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms single-modality baselines, achieving AUCs of 0.9147 and 0.9479, respectively. Ablation studies further validate the effectiveness of both the multi-stage interaction design and the multimodal fusion strategy. These results suggest that integrating pre- and post-treatment imaging with clinical notes can improve prognostic performance, providing a practical solution for individualized outcome prediction in AIS patients following EVT.

title: Contralateral DTI-ALPS index as a prognostic biomarker in IDH-wildtype glioblastoma: integrating extent of resection and sex-stratified analyses.
abstract: Aim This study aimed to evaluate the independent prognostic value of the contralateral DTI-ALPS index in IDH-wildtype glioblastoma, incorporating tumor morphometry, extent of resection, and sex-stratified analyses within a multivariable framework. Methods A retrospective analysis was performed on 153 IDH-wildtype glioblastoma patients from the publicly available UPENN-GBM dataset. Contralateral DTI-ALPS was calculated using DSI Studio via manual ROI placement; tumor morphometry was derived from expert-annotated segmentation labels using 3D Slicer. Survival analyses included Kaplan-Meier estimation, multivariable Cox regression, time-dependent ROC, restricted cubic spline, and sequential C-index comparison with likelihood-ratio testing. Results The contralateral DTI-ALPS index independently predicted overall survival after adjustment for age, sex, tumor volume, and GTR status (HR = 0.405, 95% CI: 0.227-0.725, p = 0.002). Each one standard deviation increase in DTI-ALPS was associated with a 24.2% reduction in mortality risk. GTR ≥ 90% (HR = 0.651, p = 0.017) and age (HR = 1.021, p = 0.007) also retained independent significance. DTI-ALPS significantly improved model discrimination beyond age alone (C-index: 0.625 → 0.653 → 0.668; likelihood-ratio test p = 0.002). Time-dependent AUC reached 0.741 at 6 months. ALPS-based stratification was more pronounced in the subtotal resection subgroup. Sex-stratified analyses showed numerically stronger associations in females, but formal interaction testing did not confirm effect modification. In an exploratory MGMT subset (n = 57), DTI-ALPS did not retain independent significance after MGMT adjustment. Conclusion The contralateral DTI-ALPS index may provide complementary prognostic information beyond established clinical predictors in IDH-wildtype glioblastoma; however, given the incomplete MGMT methylation data and ongoing methodological debate regarding the biological validity of DTI-ALPS, these findings should be considered exploratory. Prospective validation in cohorts with complete molecular and treatment data is required.

title: Diagnostic value of 3D pCASL perfusion in glioma grading according to the WHO 2021 classification: a retrospective study of 530 cases.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate the diagnostic performance of three-dimensional pseudo-continuous arterial spin labeling (3D pCASL) for preoperative grading of gliomas within the 2021 WHO classification framework and to assess protocol-specific tumor blood flow thresholds for differentiating CNS WHO grade 2 from grade 3-4 tumors. Methods This retrospective single-center study included 530 patients with newly diagnosed supratentorial glial tumors examined between 2011 and 2024. Nineteen non-diffuse CNS WHO grade 1 tumors were retained for descriptive purposes only and excluded from all grading analyses; the primary analytical cohort therefore comprised 511 gliomas (grade 2, n = 75; grade 3, n = 152; grade 4, n = 284). Diagnoses were reassigned within the WHO 2021 framework using the histological and molecular information available for each patient; tumors lacking molecular information required for an integrated WHO diagnosis were designated NOS. All patients underwent 3.0 T MRI with 3D pCASL. Maximum tumor blood flow (maxTBF) and normalized TBF relative to white matter (nTBF WM) and gray matter (nTBF GM) were measured using approximately 30-mm² hotspot ROIs. Results In gliomas, maxTBF, nTBF WM, and nTBF GM differentiated grade 2 from grade 3-4 tumors, with AUCs of 0.848, 0.833, and 0.84, respectively. The maxTBF threshold was 63.3 mL/100 g/min; AUCs were 0.743-0.768 for grade 2 versus grade 3 and 0.668-0.715 for grade 3 versus grade 4. After exclusion of NOS cases, glioblastomas and grade 4 astrocytomas did not differ significantly in maxTBF or nTBF (pfdr > 0.05). 3D pCASL also differentiated non-enhancing glioblastomas from grade 2 astrocytomas (maxTBF, pfdr = 0.0018; nTBF, pfdr = 0.0036-0.006), with AUCs of 0.78-0.86, a maxTBF cutoff of 64.1 mL/100 g/min, and specificity up to 96%. maxTBF and nTBF moderately correlated with Ki-67 (r = 0.44-0.50; pfdr < 0.001). Conclusions 3D pCASL provides high diagnostic accuracy for differentiating grade 2 gliomas from high-grade gliomas and grade 2 from grade 3 tumors within the WHO 2021 framework, while remaining fully non-invasive and requiring no contrast agent.

title: Real-world performance and misclassification patterns of deep learning for intracranial hemorrhage detection.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate the real-world diagnostic accuracy and systematic misclassification patterns of a deep learning algorithm (Hevi AI) for detecting intracranial hemorrhage (ICH) on non-contrast head computed tomography (CT) within a single-center cohort. Methods This retrospective, single-center study included 1,617 emergency non-contrast head CT examinations. Two expert radiologists served as the reference standard. The algorithm's binary detection performance (sensitivity, specificity, negative predictive value [NPV]) and subtyping accuracy were analyzed. Statistical analyses evaluated age and sex differences between false-positive (FP) and true-negative (TN) cases. Results The reference standard ICH prevalence was 13.4% (n = 218). The algorithm demonstrated 98.17% sensitivity, 94.71% specificity and 99.70% NPV for hemorrhage detection. Specificity demonstrated an inverse relationship with patient age (96.95% in < 50 years, 93.04% in 50-70 years, and 88.54% in > 70 years). Among 74 FP cases, isolated subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) was the most frequent misclassification (62.16%). The mean age of FP cases (56.3 ± 22.3 years) was significantly higher than that of TN cases (40.5 ± 25.2 years) (p < 0.001). Subtyping errors (n = 96) predominantly showed an "over-labeling" pattern: 49 cases (51.0%) involved unnecessary epidural hemorrhage components added to subdural hemorrhages, and 31 cases (32.3%) involved unnecessary SAH additions. Conclusions While the Hevi AI algorithm demonstrates high sensitivity and an excellent NPV that support its utility in worklist prioritization, it exhibits specific neuroanatomical blind spots. Ischemic processes, vasogenic edema, and age-related structural changes are major sources of FP alerts. Furthermore, the algorithm systematically struggles to differentiate fine extra-axial boundaries, leading to over-labeling. Recognizing these specific failure patterns and geriatric variations is essential for safe clinical integration and accurate interpretation of AI-assisted neuroimaging.

title: CT Perfusion in the differential diagnosis of glioblastomas and primary central nervous system lymphomas.
abstract: Purpose To compare perfusion parameters of glioblastomas and primary central nervous system lymphomas (PCNSL) using CT perfusion (CTP) and to assess the diagnostic performance of this technique for their preoperative differential diagnosis. Methods This single-center retrospective study included CTP data from 122 patients (57 with PCNSL and 65 with glioblastoma) examined at our hospital between 2006 and 2026. All diagnoses were histologically verified; no patient received chemotherapy, corticosteroids or radiotherapy prior to CTP. Imaging was performed on a 64-slice Optima 660 scanner (GE Medical Systems) using a prolonged perfusion protocol. Absolute (CBF, CBV, MTT, PS) and normalized (nCBF, nCBV, nMTT, nPS) perfusion parameters were obtained. The Mann-Whitney U test, Spearman correlation and ROC analysis were applied for statistical comparison. Results Glioblastomas demonstrated significantly higher CBF and CBV and lower MTT and PS values than PCNSL; the same pattern was observed for the normalized parameters. PS (AUC = 0.93), nPS (AUC = 0.90), nCBF (AUC = 0.91), nCBV (AUC = 0.90), CBF (AUC = 0.88) and CBV (AUC = 0.88) showed the highest diagnostic performance, whereas MTT and nMTT were less informative (AUC = 0.69-0.72). Conclusion CTP is a highly informative non-invasive quantitative imaging tool for the preoperative differentiation of glioblastomas and PCNSL. The inclusion of normalized perfusion parameters improves reproducibility and supports use in routine clinical practice and multicenter studies. CTP can be recommended whenever conventional CT and MRI fail to reliably distinguish these tumors.

title: Sylviocentral ratio: a novel magnetic resonance imaging marker for differentiating probable idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus from diffuse cerebral atrophy.
abstract: Purpose Probable idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus (pNPH) is a potentially treatable neurological disorder that can be difficult to differentiate from diffuse cerebral atrophy because of overlapping clinical and imaging features. This study evaluated the diagnostic performance of a novel magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-derived marker, the sylviocentral ratio, for distinguishing pNPH from diffuse cerebral atrophy. Methods In this prospective study, 72 patients (36 with pNPH and 36 with diffuse cerebral atrophy) underwent routine brain MRI, with an additional sagittal 3D T2-weighted SPACE acquisition; axial and coronal reformatted images were generated from the volumetric dataset for standardized measurements. Sylvian fissure and central sulcus diameters were measured on these standardized images using predefined anatomical landmarks, and the sylviocentral ratio was calculated. Results The sylviocentral ratio was significantly higher in patients with pNPH than in those with diffuse cerebral atrophy (10.94 ± 4.67 vs. 2.86 ± 2.00, p < 0.001). Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis demonstrated excellent diagnostic performance, with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.953 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.896-0.994). A cut-off value of ≥ 5.3 yielded a sensitivity of 91.7% and a specificity of 94.4%. Diagnostic performance was comparable to the callosal angle (AUC = 0.951) and superior to the Evans index (AUC = 0.922). The sylviocentral ratio remained independently associated with pNPH after adjustment for age (p < 0.001). Interobserver agreement was excellent (intraclass correlation coefficient [ICC] = 0.94). Conclusion The sylviocentral ratio is a practical, reproducible, and highly accurate MRI marker for differentiating pNPH from diffuse cerebral atrophy and may complement established imaging parameters in clinical assessment. Given the limited size of the age-matched cohort, validation in larger, ideally external cohorts is warranted before widespread clinical implementation.

title: Partial injury of the triradiate cartilage following low-energy trauma.
abstract: Background Acute traumatic injuries of the triradiate cartilage are very rare in children and usually result from high-energy trauma associated with other pelvic injuries. Only two sports-related cases of complete injuries of the triradiate cartilage have been reported to date. Case presentation We herein describe the first case of a partial injury of the triradiate cartilage in a 14-year-old athlete. The patient presented with sudden-onset hip pain and moderate functional impairment. The fracture was confined to the ilioischial synchondrosis, while the remaining triradiate cartilage and the contralateral side were fused. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) suggested the diagnosis, which was confirmed by a computed tomography (CT) scanner. Conclusion This case highlights the importance of carefully evaluating the triradiate cartilage on imaging in young athletes with sudden-onset hip pain, even when the triradiate cartilage remains partially open unilaterally.

title: Thrombosed mycotic aneurysm of the cervical internal carotid artery mimicking a parapharyngeal abscess in a child: a case report of multimodal imaging diagnosis.
abstract: A parapharyngeal abscess, although relatively rare, is a potentially life-threatening deep neck space infection in the pediatric population that carries a risk of serious complications. Mycotic pseudoaneurysm of the cervical internal carotid artery (ICA) is a rare vascular complication in children that can lead to catastrophic hemorrhage if misdiagnosed and attempted for surgical incision. We report a 7-year-old malnourished boy presenting with fever, dysphagia, and neck stiffness. Suboptimal contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) suggested a left parapharyngeal abscess, and surgical drainage was planned. A dedicated CT, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) with diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) and apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) mapping, magnetic resonance angiography, and three-dimensional CT angiography identified a completely thrombosed mycotic pseudoaneurysm rather than an abscess. This case demonstrates that complete thrombosis transforms a mycotic pseudoaneurysm into a mass that can easily be mistaken for an abscess without the right imaging modalities and high-quality imaging.

This case demonstrates that complete thrombosis transforms a mycotic pseudoaneurysm into a mass that can easily be mistaken for an abscess without the right imaging modalities and high-quality imaging.

title: Deep learning-based synthetic CT for the assessment of spinal structural lesions in axial spondyloarthritis.
abstract: Objective To evaluate the accuracy of synthetic CT for detecting spinal structural lesions in patients with suspected axial spondyloarthritis (axSpA). Materials and methods Patients with inflammatory back pain who underwent both spinal CT and MRI examinations were included in this retrospective study. Two readers independently assessed the presence of structural lesions (facet joint ankylosis, structural Andersson lesions, discal ossifications, vertebral ankylosis, syndesmophytes, and erosions) on conventional CT and synthetic CT images. Feature detection accuracy of synthetic CT relative to conventional CT was evaluated using sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, and negative predictive value, with consensus reading as the reference standard. In addition, lesion-level erosion detection accuracy was assessed, and erosion size was compared between conventional CT and synthetic CT. Results Eighty-seven patients (mean age, 41 ± 14.2 years; range, 18-80 years; 42 males and 45 females) were included. Sensitivity of synthetic CT was 1.00 for facet joint ankylosis, structural Andersson lesions, vertebral ankylosis, and erosions, 0.91 for syndesmophytes, and 0.67 for discal ossifications. Specificity ranged from 0.97 to 1.00 across all lesion types. Lesion-level analysis showed sensitivity of 0.82-1.00 and specificity of 0.96-1.00 for erosion detection across different spinal regions. No significant differences of erosion size (median [IQR], mm) between conventional CT and synthetic CT (width, 7.7 [4.4-9.7] vs. 8.0 [4.1-9.6], P = 0.15; depth, 4.5 [3.5-6.7] vs. 4.5 [3.5-6.5], P = 0.12). Conclusion Synthetic CT demonstrates a high feature detection accuracy for assessing most spinal structural lesions in patients with suspected axSpA.

title: Applications and performance of imaging artificial intelligence in detecting and staging avascular necrosis of the femoral head: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Objective To evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of imaging artificial intelligence (AI) models for detecting avascular necrosis of the femoral head (AVNFH) and to examine whether diagnostic performance differs according to imaging modality, disease-stage focus, and validation strategy. Materials and methods In accordance with PRISMA-DTA, we conducted a systematic search in four main databases. Two independent reviewers evaluated the studies, extracted relevant data, and assessed the quality following the QUADAS-2 criteria. The primary analysis pooled overall sensitivity and specificity using a bivariate random-effects model. Prespecified subgroup analyses assessed differences by imaging modality, disease stage focus, and evaluation strategy. Results Nine selected estimates contributed to the primary analysis of binary AVNFH detection. Pooled sensitivity was 0.888 (95% CI, 0.789-0.944), specificity was 0.937 (95% CI, 0.906-0.958), and SROC AUC was 0.967. MRI-based estimates showed higher sensitivity than radiography-based estimates in the study-level comparison (p = 0.027). No significant subgroup differences were found by disease-stage focus and validation strategy (all p > 0.05). Only five external test-set estimates contributed to the primary analysis; subgroup comparisons had limited precision. Conclusion Imaging AI models showed promising accuracy for AVNFH detection in research datasets. However, risk of bias, between-study heterogeneity, and limited external testing restrict confidence in their clinical applicability. Prospective, multicenter validation and evaluation of clinical benefit are needed before routine implementation.

title: Age- and sex-specific values of regional bone mineral density from opportunistic CT of the lower lumbar spine, pelvis, sacrum, and proximal femur.
abstract: Objective Standard osteoporosis assessment using dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) provides limited 2D measures (BMD, T-score), potentially missing localized bone density differences relevant to fracture risk. Opportunistic CT allows comprehensive 3D volumetric bone density analysis. This study presents a detailed 3D statistical model of CT-derived apparent volumetric bone mineral density (CT-vBMD) covering the L4 and L5 vertebrae, pelvic bones, sacrum, and proximal femur and examines spatial distributions and associations with age and sex. Materials and methods Retrospective analysis included 330 routine abdominal CT scans (ages 20-91; approximately balanced by sex). Bones were segmented with a semi-automated workflow, internally calibrated, registered to bone-specific population templates, and projected onto corresponding tetrahedral meshes. Whole-bone averages were compared across age groups and between sexes. For each element, we calculated mean vBMD, variability, correlations with age and sex, and cluster-defined low-density and age-sensitive subregions. Results The global spatial pattern was similar in females and males. The highest CT-vBMD values were localized mainly to cortical load-bearing zones, whereas the lowest values were concentrated in trabecular spongiosa. Older age was associated with lower whole-bone CT-vBMD in all bones and with stronger negative associations in trabecular-rich regions, such as the subchondral acetabulum, femoral neck, sacral ala, and vertebral bodies. Cortical-dominant load-bearing regions showed weaker negative associations with age. Conclusion This framework maps anatomically localized associations between age and CT-vBMD beyond the regions routinely assessed by DXA. Opportunistic CT mapping may complement standard osteoporosis assessment by providing spatial information for the pelvis, sacrum, lower lumbar spine, and proximal femur.

title: Regional variation in vertebral bone marrow adiposity: a population-based atlas of age- and sex-specific patterns.
abstract: Background Bone marrow adipose tissue (BMAT) is a metabolically active fat depot implicated in skeletal aging and systemic metabolism. While chemical shift-encoding MRI enables noninvasive quantification of bone marrow fat fraction (BMFF), current knowledge of vertebral BMAT is largely limited to small cohorts or restricted anatomical regions. Purpose To characterize the spatial distribution of vertebral bone marrow fat fraction across the spine and determine region-specific associations with age and sex in a population-based cohort. Materials and methods In this retrospective study, MRI data from 82,920 UK Biobank participants recruited between 2006 and 2010 were analyzed. The baseline case subset (n = 81,318) had a mean age of 54.8 ± 7.6 years, and 42,113/81,318 (51.8%) were female. Automated vertebral body segmentation enabled voxel-wise BMFF quantification using Dixon MRI. Vertebra- and region-level BMFF metrics were derived. Associations with age and sex were assessed using region-specific linear regression. Results Vertebral BMAT demonstrated a non-linear cranio-caudal pattern. Mean BMFF was ~ 39% in the cervical, ~ 55% in the thoracic, ~ 45% in the lumbar spine, and ~ 70% in the sacrum. BMAT increased with age in all regions (all p < 0.001; increase per decade: cervical 3.33%, thoracic 3.41%, lumbar 2.95%, sacral 3.83%). Females exhibited higher BMFF than males across all regions (all p < 0.001). The overall spatial pattern remained consistent across age groups and sexes. Conclusion Vertebral BMAT exhibits a structured, non-linear spatial distribution with region-specific age- and sex-dependent patterns. This population-based atlas provides normative reference data supporting region-specific BMAT assessment in skeletal and metabolic disease.

title: Dual-energy CT virtual non-calcium imaging for differentiating pathologic from non-pathologic femoral fractures: a study of inexperienced non-radiologist readers.
abstract: Objective To assess the effect of dual-energy CT (DECT) virtual non-calcium (VNCa) imaging on the ability of inexperienced non-radiologist readers to differentiate pathologic from non-pathologic femoral fractures. Materials and methods In this retrospective diagnostic accuracy study, 45 eligible emergency department patients with femoral fractures who underwent DECT between January 2022 and September 2024 were included, comprising 20 patients with pathologic fractures and 25 with non-pathologic fractures. The reference standard for fracture classification was established using surgical records or histopathologic results. Two inexperienced non-radiologist readers independently evaluated conventional CT alone and conventional CT combined with color-coded DECT VNCa images in separate reading sessions. Sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) were compared between the two sessions. AUCs were compared using the paired DeLong test. Results The addition of DECT VNCa significantly improved sensitivity for detecting pathologic fractures in both readers. For Reader 1, sensitivity increased from 65 to 95% (p = 0.031), and accuracy increased from 77.8% to 95.6%. For Reader 2, sensitivity increased from 50 to 85% (p = 0.016), and accuracy increased from 68.9% to 91.1%. Specificity remained high without significant differences between sessions. AUC increased from 0.765 (95% CI, 0.617-0.913) to 0.955 (95% CI, 0.883-1.0) for Reader 1 and from 0.670 (95% CI, 0.506-0.834) to 0.905 (95% CI, 0.802-1.0) for Reader 2 (p = 0.0135 and < 0.01, respectively). Conclusion Adding color-coded DECT VNCa to conventional CT improves the diagnostic performance of inexperienced non-radiologist readers in detecting pathologic femoral fractures.

title: Clinical evaluation of deep learning-based acquisition and reconstruction techniques for accelerated 2D shoulder magnetic resonance imaging acceleration at 3 T.
abstract: Purpose GE has recently developed Sonic DL MRI acceleration technology. We wished to (1) quantify scanner time reduction compared to the AIR Recon DL already in clinical use at our institution and (2) preliminarily evaluate any change in diagnostic findings between these methods. Methods A total of 30 outpatients undergoing routine shoulder MRI for shoulder pain were recruited. Each underwent routine AIR Recon DL and Sonic DL exams containing the same sequences. Three subspecialized musculoskeletal radiologists assessed image quality, graded pathology, and reported diagnostic confidence in a blinded fashion. Differences in image quality and confidence were compared using Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. Results Sonic DL reduced nominal acquisition time 38.7% compared to AIR Recon DL (6 min 15 s versus 10 min 12 s). Artifact was considered slightly worse on the routine examination (3.20 versus 3.37, P = 0.039); there was no significant difference in image quality, sharpness, or signal-to-noise ratio between routine and Sonic DL accelerated exams (P 0.171-0.861). Inter-reader agreement was broadly similar between routine-routine and routine-Sonic DL comparisons (median agreement 0.867 and 0.839, respectively). Within-reader analysis identified subacromial/subdeltoid bursitis and supraspinatus tendon tears more frequently on the routine protocol than on Sonic DL (P 0.049 and P 0.006, respectively). Conclusion Sonic DL enabled a 38.7% reduction in nominal shoulder MRI acquisition time with broadly comparable image quality and inter-reader agreement in this pilot cohort. Diagnostic equivalence was not established; subacromial/subdeltoid bursitis and supraspinatus tears were potentially less conspicuous on Sonic DL. A larger powered validation study would be needed to fully evaluate diagnostic performance.

Purpose

GE has recently developed Sonic DL MRI acceleration technology. We wished to (1) quantify scanner time reduction compared to the AIR Recon DL already in clinical use at our institution and (2) preliminarily evaluate any change in diagnostic findings between these methods.

Methods

A total of 30 outpatients undergoing routine shoulder MRI for shoulder pain were recruited. Each underwent routine AIR Recon DL and Sonic DL exams containing the same sequences. Three subspecialized musculoskeletal radiologists assessed image quality, graded pathology, and reported diagnostic confidence in a blinded fashion. Differences in image quality and confidence were compared using Wilcoxon signed-rank tests.

Results

Sonic DL reduced nominal acquisition time 38.7% compared to AIR Recon DL (6 min 15 s versus 10 min 12 s). Artifact was considered slightly worse on the routine examination (3.20 versus 3.37, P = 0.039); there was no significant difference in image quality, sharpness, or signal-to-noise ratio between routine and Sonic DL accelerated exams (P 0.171-0.861). Inter-reader agreement was broadly similar between routine-routine and routine-Sonic DL comparisons (median agreement 0.867 and 0.839, respectively). Within-reader analysis identified subacromial/subdeltoid bursitis and supraspinatus tendon tears more frequently on the routine protocol than on Sonic DL (P 0.049 and P 0.006, respectively).

Conclusion

Sonic DL enabled a 38.7% reduction in nominal shoulder MRI acquisition time with broadly comparable image quality and inter-reader agreement in this pilot cohort. Diagnostic equivalence was not established; subacromial/subdeltoid bursitis and supraspinatus tears were potentially less conspicuous on Sonic DL. A larger powered validation study would be needed to fully evaluate diagnostic performance.

title: A case report of pediatric Gardner syndrome and literature review.
abstract: This case report discusses the diagnosis and treatment of a 14-year-8-month-old male patient genetically diagnosed with Gardner syndrome (GS), systematically reviewing the disease's epidemiology, clinical manifestations, imaging advances, and management strategies. The patient presented with a post-influenza A chest wall mass and had prior resections of abdominal/scalp masses. Colonoscopy revealed > 20 adenomatous polyps. Imaging demonstrated multiple craniofacial osteomas and epidermoid cysts. Genetic testing identified a pathogenic APC gene mutation (NM_000038.6:c.4669_4670del (p.Ile1557*) heterozygous variant). GS, a familial adenomatous polyposis (FAP) subtype, has an estimated pediatric incidence of 1/8000-1/14,000. Its classic triad comprises colorectal polyps, osteomas, and soft tissue tumors. Recent studies indicate earlier malignant transformation of duodenal polyps in children versus adults, with desmoid tumor incidence reaching 10-20%. In imaging, low-dose CT, panoramic radiography, and contrast-enhanced MRI can improve early detection of bone lesions and soft tissue tumors. Genetic testing (APC/MUTYH) is the pediatric screening gold standard. Optimized chemoprevention (sulindac/celecoxib) and endoscopic monitoring have significantly improved prognoses. This case highlights the urgency of multidisciplinary management and genetic counseling for pediatric GS.

title: Primary leiomyosarcoma arising adjacent to a femoral stem following total hip arthroplasty: a case report with radiologic and histopathological correlation.
abstract: Periprosthetic sarcomas associated with total hip arthroplasty (THA) are exceedingly rare, and most reported cases represent undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma or osteosarcoma. Primary leiomyosarcoma of bone is also an uncommon malignancy, accounting for less than 1% of primary malignant bone tumors. The occurrence of primary leiomyosarcoma adjacent to an orthopedic implant is therefore exceptionally rare. A 69-year-old woman presented with progressive left thigh pain 13 years after THA. Radiographs demonstrated osteolysis and cortical thinning at the distal femoral stem. Computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) revealed an intramedullary lesion with cortical thinning and contrast enhancement. 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography-CT showed increased uptake at the lesion (SUV max, 11.9), without evidence of other primary tumors. The differential diagnoses included implant-related osteolysis, infection, metastatic tumor, and primary bone tumor. An open biopsy was performed, and a diagnosis of pleomorphic sarcoma was made. Wide resection with proximal femoral replacement was performed. Histopathological examination established the diagnosis of primary leiomyosarcoma of bone. Prominent lymphocytic infiltration and immunohistochemical findings, including p53 overexpression and partial loss of Rb expression, within the tumor, raise the possibility of chronic inflammation and associated molecular alterations as theoretical contributing factors to tumorigenesis. Periprosthetic sarcomas can mimic more common postoperative complications, making diagnosis challenging. Delayed diagnosis may adversely affect prognosis. This case highlights the importance of considering malignancy in atypical periprosthetic lesions and underscores the role of multimodality imaging and biopsy in achieving an accurate diagnosis.

title: IgG4-related disease of the pelvic floor musculature mimicking neoplasm: a case report with imaging-pathologic correlation.
abstract: IgG4-related disease (IgG4-RD) is an immune-mediated fibroinflammatory condition that can form tumefactive mass-like lesions and mimic malignancy across organ systems. We describe a rare presentation involving the deep pelvic floor musculature with imaging-pathologic correlation while underscoring diagnostic pitfalls. A 49-year-old man with a history of systemic lupus erythematosus, night sweats, and left lower quadrant abdominal pain underwent CT of the abdomen and pelvis, which demonstrated a right posterior pelvic sidewall mass and retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy. Pelvic MRI demonstrated an ill-defined intramuscular mass centered in the right iliococcygeus and pubococcygeus muscles. Relative to skeletal muscle, the lesion demonstrated iso- to low T1 signal intensity, intermediate T2 signal intensity, restricted diffusion, and moderate, diffuse contrast enhancement, raising concern for neoplasm or an inflammatory process. Image-guided biopsy revealed fibrotic soft tissue with severe lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate and increased IgG4-reactive plasma cells. The IgG4+/IgG+ plasma cell ratio was > 75%, consistent with IgG4-RD when integrated with the clinical, laboratory, imaging and pathologic findings. IgG4-related disease with mass-like involvement of the pelvic floor musculature has not, to the best of our knowledge, been previously reported in the English literature. This entity can present as an ill-defined, enhancing, diffusion-restricting intramuscular mass and therefore may mimic a neoplastic process.

title: A rare case of bilateral cuboid-navicular coalitions.
abstract: Cuboid-navicular coalitions are an exceptionally rare form of tarsal coalitions, representing less than 1% of all tarsal coalitions. Although tarsal coalitions classically become symptomatic during adolescence, cuboid-navicular coalitions may remain clinically silent until adulthood and can present with nonspecific chronic midfoot or hindfoot pain. We present a rare case of bilateral cuboid-navicular coalitions in a 42-year-old man with progressive bilateral midfoot pain, associated degenerative hindfoot and midfoot changes, and bilateral peroneal tendon pathology. Initial management consisted of orthotics, bracing, and nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, but symptoms progressed over 8 years. Cross-sectional imaging demonstrated bilateral cuboid-navicular coalitions, progressive degenerative changes, and high-grade right peroneus longus tear. The patient underwent excision of the right cuboid-navicular coalition, excision of the right lateral calcaneal tubercle with inferior peroneal retinacular release, and debridement and repair of the right peroneus longus and brevis tendons. This case highlights the importance of considering rare tarsal coalitions in adults with chronic nonspecific midfoot pain and emphasizes the value of MRI and CT for diagnosis, characterization of associated pathology, and operative planning.
